sentences.zh: 【梁紀十一】　起重光大淵獻，盡玄黓困敦，凡二年。

translations.literal: [Liang Records 11] From Chongguang Dayuanyuan to Xuanyi Kundun; two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Liang Records 11] The cycle runs from Chongguang Dayuanyuan through Xuanyi Kundun; two years in all.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝十一中大通三年（

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang, year eleven of Zhongdatong (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang, year eleven of Zhongdatong (

sentences.zh: 辛亥，公元五三一年）

translations.literal: xinchai, 531 CE)
translations.idiomatic: xinchai, 531 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛巳，上祀南郊，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on xinsi, the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on xinsi, the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 魏尚書右僕射鄭先護聞洛陽不守，士眾逃散，遂來奔。

translations.literal: Wei's Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Right Deputy Director Zheng Xianhu, hearing that Luoyang was lost and troops and people had scattered in flight, came over to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei's Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Right Deputy Director Zheng Xianhu, heard that Luoyang had fallen and troops and people had scattered, he came over to surrender.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以先護為征北大將軍。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Xianhu was made Grand General Who Campaigns North.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Xianhu was appointed Grand General Who Campaigns North.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛丑，上祀明堂。

translations.literal: In the second month, on xinchou, the emperor sacrificed at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinchou, the emperor sacrificed at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 魏自敬宗被囚，宮室空近百日。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Jingzong of Wei was imprisoned, the palace had stood empty for nearly a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Jingzong of Wei had been imprisoned, the palace had stood empty for nearly a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 爾朱世隆鎮洛陽，商旅流通，盜賊不作。

translations.literal: Erzhu Shilong held Luoyang; merchants and travelers moved freely, and bandits did not arise.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong held Luoyang; merchants and travelers moved freely, and bandits did not arise.

sentences.zh: 世隆兄弟密議，以長廣王疏遠，又無人望，欲更立近親。

translations.literal: Shilong and his brothers met in secret. They thought the Prince of Changgung was remote in kinship and lacked popular esteem, and wished to enthrone someone nearer in blood.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong and his brothers met in secret. The Prince of Changgung was remote in kinship and lacked popular esteem; they wished to enthrone someone nearer in blood.

sentences.zh: 儀同三司廣陵王恭，羽之子也，好學有志度，正光中領給事黃門侍郎，以元叉擅權，托瘖病居龍華佛寺，無所交通。

translations.literal: Guangling Wang Gong, Bearer of the Staff with Equal Rank to the Three Dukes, was a son of Yu. He loved learning and had resolve and measure. In the Zhengguang era he served as Supervisor of Attendants in the Yellow Gate. Because Yuan Cha monopolized power, he feigned muteness and illness and lived at Longhua Buddhist Temple, associating with no one.
translations.idiomatic: Guangling Wang Gong, Bearer of the Staff with Equal Rank to the Three Dukes, was a son of Yu. He loved learning and had resolve and measure. In the Zhengguang era he served as Supervisor of Attendants in the Yellow Gate. Because Yuan Cha monopolized power, he feigned muteness and illness and lived at Longhua Buddhist Temple, associating with no one.

sentences.zh: 永安末，有白敬宗言王陽瘖，將有異志。

translations.literal: Late in the Yongan era someone reported to Jingzong that the prince only pretended to be mute and harbored rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Yongan era someone reported to Jingzong that the prince only pretended to be mute and harbored rebellious intent.

sentences.zh: 恭懼，逃於上洛山，洛州刺史執送之，系治久之，以無狀獲免。

translations.literal: Gong was afraid, fled to Mount Shangluo, was seized by the Luozhou inspector and sent back, and was imprisoned for a long time before being released when nothing was proved against him.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was afraid, fled to Mount Shangluo, was seized by the Luozhou inspector and sent back, and was imprisoned for a long time before being released when nothing was proved against him.

sentences.zh: 關西大行台郎中薛孝通說爾朱天光曰：「廣陵王，高祖猶子，夙有令望，沉晦不言，多歷年所。

translations.literal: Xue Xiaotong, a gentleman of the Western Guanxi Grand Commissioner, said to Erzhu Tianguang, "Guangling Wang is a grandson of Emperor Gaozu of Wei. He has long enjoyed a fine reputation and has kept silent and withdrawn for many years.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Xiaotong, a gentleman of the Western Guanxi Grand Commissioner, said to Erzhu Tianguang, "Guangling Wang is a grandson of Emperor Gaozu of Wei. He has long enjoyed a fine reputation and has kept silent and withdrawn for many years.

sentences.zh: 若奉以為主，必天人允葉。

translations.literal: If you set him up as sovereign, Heaven and men will surely be of one mind."
translations.idiomatic: If you set him up as sovereign, Heaven and men will surely be of one mind."

sentences.zh: 」天光與世隆等謀之，疑其實瘖，使爾朱彥伯潛往敦諭，且脅之，恭乃曰：「天何言哉！

translations.literal: Tianguang and Shilong and the others plotted together. They doubted he was truly mute and sent Erzhu Yanbo in secret to persuade and also threaten him. Gong then said, "What words has Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang, Shilong, and the others plotted together. Doubting that he was truly mute, they sent Erzhu Yanbo in secret to persuade and threaten him. Gong then said, "What words has Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 」世隆等大喜。

translations.literal: Shilong and the others were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong and the others were greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 孝通，聰之子也。

translations.literal: Xiaotong was a son of Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaotong was a son of Cong.

sentences.zh: 己巳，長廣王至邙山南，世隆等為之作禪文，使泰山太守遼西竇瑗執鞭獨入，啟長廣王曰：「天人之望，皆在廣陵，願行堯、舜之事。

translations.literal: On jisi, the Prince of Changgung arrived south of Mount Mang. Shilong and the others drew up an abdication document for him and had Liaodong native Dou Yuan, Administrator of Mount Tai, enter alone with a whip and address the Prince of Changgung: "Heaven and men's hopes all rest on Guangling. We beg you to do as Yao and Shun did."
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, the Prince of Changgung arrived south of Mount Mang. Shilong and the others drew up an abdication document for him and had Dou Yuan of Liaodong, Administrator of Mount Tai, enter alone with a whip and address the Prince of Changgung: "Heaven and men's hopes all rest on Guangling. We beg you to do as Yao and Shun did."

sentences.zh: 」遂署禪文。

translations.literal: He then signed the abdication document.
translations.idiomatic: He then signed the abdication document.

sentences.zh: 廣陵王奉表三讓，然後即位。

translations.literal: Guangling Wang submitted a memorial thrice declining, then took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Guangling Wang submitted a memorial thrice declining, then took the throne.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元普泰。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to Putai.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to Putai.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎邢子才為赦文，敘敬宗枉殺太原王榮之狀，節閔帝曰：「永安手翦強臣，非為失德，直以天未厭亂，故逢成濟之禍耳。

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Gentleman Xing Zicai drafted the amnesty text, recounting how Jingzong had wrongly killed the Prince of Taiyuan, Rong. Emperor Jiemin said, "In the Yongan era I personally cut down a powerful minister. That was not loss of virtue; it was only that Heaven had not yet tired of disorder, and so I met the disaster of Cheng Ji."
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate Gentleman Xing Zicai drafted the amnesty text, recounting how Jingzong had wrongly killed the Prince of Taiyuan, Rong. Emperor Jiemin said, "In the Yongan era I personally cut down a powerful minister. That was not loss of virtue; it was only that Heaven had not yet tired of disorder, and so I met the disaster of Cheng Ji."

sentences.zh: 」因顧左右取筆，自作赦文，直言：「門下：朕以寡德，運屬樂推，思與億兆，同茲大慶，肆眚之科，一依常式。

translations.literal: He then turned to those at his side for a brush and wrote the amnesty himself, saying plainly: "To the Secretariat: We, of meager virtue, have been borne on the tide of popular acclaim. We wish to share this great rejoicing with the hundred million. The scope of pardon shall follow the usual form."
translations.idiomatic: He then turned to those at his side for a brush and wrote the amnesty himself, saying plainly: "To the Secretariat: We, of meager virtue, have been borne on the tide of popular acclaim. We wish to share this great rejoicing with the hundred million. The scope of pardon shall follow the usual form."

sentences.zh: 」帝閉口八年，至是乃言，中外欣然，以為明主，望至太平。

translations.literal: The emperor had kept silent for eight years; only now did he speak. Within and without the court rejoiced, taking him for a clear-sighted ruler and hoping for great peace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had kept silent for eight years; only now did he speak. Within and without the court rejoiced, taking him for a clear-sighted ruler and hoping for great peace.

sentences.zh: 庚午，詔以「三皇稱『皇』，五帝稱『帝』，三代稱『王』，蓋遞為沖挹；

translations.literal: On gengwu an edict said, "The Three Sovereigns were called 'Sovereign,' the Five Emperors were called 'Emperor,' and the Three Dynasties were called 'King'—each title a step down in self-effacement;
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu an edict said, "The Three Sovereigns were called 'Sovereign,' the Five Emperors were called 'Emperor,' and the Three Dynasties were called 'King'—each title a step down in self-effacement;

sentences.zh: 自秦以來，競稱『皇帝』，予今但稱『帝』，亦已褒矣。

translations.literal: since Qin, all have vied to call themselves 'Emperor.' We now will only be called 'Emperor'—that is already praise enough."
translations.idiomatic: since Qin, all have vied to call themselves 'Emperor.' We now will only be called 'Emperor'—that is already praise enough."

sentences.zh: 加爾朱世隆儀同三司，贈爾朱榮相國、晉王，加九錫。

translations.literal: Erzhu Shilong was advanced to Bearer of the Staff with Equal Rank to the Three Dukes. Erzhu Rong was posthumously made Chancellor of State and Prince of Jin, with the Nine Bestowals added.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong was advanced to Bearer of the Staff with Equal Rank to the Three Dukes. Erzhu Rong was posthumously made Chancellor of State and Prince of Jin, with the Nine Bestowals added.

sentences.zh: 世隆使百官議榮配饗，司直劉季明曰：「若配世宗，於時無功；

translations.literal: Shilong had the hundred officials debate with which emperor Rong should share temple sacrifice. Director of Rectitude Liu Jiming said, "If paired with Emperor Shizong, he had no merit in that age;
translations.idiomatic: Shilong had the hundred officials debate with which emperor Rong should share temple sacrifice. Director of Rectitude Liu Jiming said, "If paired with Emperor Shizong, he had no merit in that age;

sentences.zh: 若配孝明，親害其母；

translations.literal: if paired with Emperor Xiaoming, he personally harmed his mother;
translations.idiomatic: if paired with Emperor Xiaoming, he personally harmed his mother;

sentences.zh: 若配莊帝，為臣不終。

translations.literal: if paired with Emperor Zhuang, as a minister he did not see things through to the end.
translations.idiomatic: if paired with Emperor Zhuang, as a minister he did not see things through to the end.

sentences.zh: 以此論之，無所可配。

translations.literal: Judged by this, there is no one with whom he can be paired."
translations.idiomatic: Judged by this, there is no one with whom he can be paired."

sentences.zh: 」世隆怒曰：「汝應死！

translations.literal: Shilong said in anger, "You deserve death!"
translations.idiomatic: Shilong said in anger, "You deserve death!"

sentences.zh: 」季明曰：「下官既為議首，依禮而言，不合聖心，翦戮唯命！

translations.literal: Jiming said, "Your subordinate was chief among those debating. Speaking according to ritual, if that does not accord with the sage heart, execution is yours to command!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiming said, "Your subordinate was chief among those debating. Speaking according to ritual, if that does not accord with the sage heart, execution is yours to command!"

sentences.zh: 」世隆亦不之罪。

translations.literal: Shilong did not punish him after all.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong did not punish him after all.

sentences.zh: 以榮配高祖廟廷。

translations.literal: Rong was paired in sacrifice at the temple of Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was paired in sacrifice at the temple of Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 又為榮立廟於首陽山，因周公舊廟而為之，以為榮功可比周公。

translations.literal: A temple was also built for Rong on Mount Shouyang, modeled on the old temple of the Duke of Zhou, on the ground that Rong's merit could be compared with the Duke of Zhou's.
translations.idiomatic: A temple was also built for Rong on Mount Shouyang, modeled on the old temple of the Duke of Zhou, on the ground that Rong's merit could be compared with the Duke of Zhou's.

sentences.zh: 廟成，尋為火所焚。

translations.literal: When the temple was completed, it was soon burned by fire.
translations.idiomatic: When the temple was completed, it was soon burned by fire.

sentences.zh: 爾朱兆以不預廢立之謀，大怒，欲攻世隆。

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhao, not having taken part in the plot to depose and enthrone, was furious and wished to attack Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao, not having taken part in the plot to depose and enthrone, was furious and wished to attack Shilong.

sentences.zh: 世隆使爾朱彥伯往諭之，乃止。

translations.literal: Shilong sent Erzhu Yanbo to explain matters to him, and Zhao stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong sent Erzhu Yanbo to explain matters to him, and Zhao stopped.

sentences.zh: 初，敬宗使安東將軍史仵龍、平北將軍陽文義各領兵三千守太行嶺，侍中源子恭鎮河內。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jingzong had sent Eastern Pacification General Shi Wulong and Pacification of the North General Yang Wenyi, each leading three thousand men, to hold the Taihang range, with Palace Attendant Yuan Zigong holding Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jingzong had sent Eastern Pacification General Shi Wulong and Pacification of the North General Yang Wenyi, each leading three thousand men, to hold the Taihang range, with Palace Attendant Yuan Zigong holding Henei.

sentences.zh: 及爾朱兆南向，仵龍、文義帥眾先降，由是子恭之軍望風亦潰，兆遂乘勝直入洛陽。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao marched south, Wulong and Wenyi led their troops to surrender first; Zigong's army likewise scattered at the sight of them. Zhao then pressed his advantage straight into Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao marched south, Wulong and Wenyi led their troops to surrender first; Zigong's army likewise scattered at the sight of them. Zhao then pressed his advantage straight into Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 至是，爾朱世隆論仵龍、文義之功，各封千戶侯。

translations.literal: At this time Shilong argued the merit of Wulong and Wenyi; each was to be enfeoffed as Marquis with a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Shilong argued the merit of Wulong and Wenyi; each was to be enfeoffed as Marquis with a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「仵龍、文義，於王有功，於國無勳。

translations.literal: The Wei sovereign said, "Wulong and Wenyi had merit toward your house but none toward the state."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei sovereign said, "Wulong and Wenyi had merit toward your house but none toward the state."

sentences.zh: 」竟不許。

translations.literal: In the end he did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not grant it.

sentences.zh: 爾朱仲遠鎮滑台，表用其下都督為西兗州刺史，先用後表。

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhongyuan held Huatai and memorialized appointing his subordinate commander as Western Yanzhou inspector, appointing first and reporting afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhongyuan held Huatai and memorialized appointing his subordinate commander as Western Yanzhou inspector, appointing first and reporting afterward.

sentences.zh: 詔答曰：「已能近補，何勞遠聞！

translations.literal: The edict in reply said, "You could fill the post nearby—why trouble us from afar!"
translations.idiomatic: The edict in reply said, "You could fill the post nearby—why trouble us from afar!"

sentences.zh: 」爾朱天光之滅-{万俟}-丑奴也，始獲波斯所獻師子，送洛陽。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Tianguang destroyed Chounu, he first obtained a lion presented by Persia and sent it to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Tianguang destroyed Chounu, he first obtained a lion presented by Persia and sent it to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及節閔帝即位，詔曰：「禽獸囚之則違其性。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jiemin took the throne, an edict said, "Beasts, if caged, go against their nature."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jiemin took the throne, an edict said, "Beasts, if caged, go against their nature."

sentences.zh: 」命送歸本國。

translations.literal: He ordered it sent back to its native land.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered it sent back to its native land.

sentences.zh: 使者以波斯道遠不可達，於路殺之而返。

translations.literal: The envoy said the road to Persia was too far to reach; on the way he killed it and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said the road to Persia was too far to reach; on the way he killed it and returned.

sentences.zh: 有司劾違旨，帝曰：「豈可以獸而罪人！

translations.literal: The authorities impeached him for disobeying the edict. The emperor said, "How can one punish a man for the sake of a beast!"
translations.idiomatic: The authorities impeached him for disobeying the edict. The emperor said, "How can one punish a man for the sake of a beast!"

sentences.zh: 」遂赦之。

translations.literal: He pardoned him in the end.
translations.idiomatic: He pardoned him in the end.

sentences.zh: 魏鎮遠將軍清河崔祖螭等聚青州七郡之眾圍東陽，旬日之間，眾十餘萬。

translations.literal: Wei Pacification General of the Farther Regions Cui Zuci of Qinghe and others gathered the forces of seven commanderies of Qingzhou and besieged Dongyang. Within ten days their numbers passed a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Pacification General of the Farther Regions Cui Zuci of Qinghe and others gathered the forces of seven commanderies of Qingzhou and besieged Dongyang. Within ten days their numbers passed a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 刺史東萊王貴平帥城民固守，使太傅咨議參軍崔光伯出城慰勞，其兄光韶曰：「城民陵縱日久，眾怒甚盛，非慰諭所能解。

translations.literal: Inspector Wang Guiping of Donglai led the townspeople in a stubborn defense and sent Grand Tutor Consultant Cui Guangbo out of the city to comfort and reassure them. His elder brother Guangshao said, "The townspeople have been insolent for many days; popular rage is very strong. Comfort and persuasion cannot resolve it.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Wang Guiping of Donglai led the townspeople in a stubborn defense and sent Grand Tutor Consultant Cui Guangbo out of the city to comfort and reassure them. His elder brother Guangshao said, "The townspeople have been insolent for many days; popular rage is very strong. Comfort and persuasion cannot resolve it.

sentences.zh: 家弟往，必不全。

translations.literal: If my younger brother goes, he will surely not return whole."
translations.idiomatic: If my younger brother goes, he will surely not return whole."

sentences.zh: 」貴平強之，既出外，人射殺之。

translations.literal: Guiping forced him to go. Once outside the city, the people shot and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Guiping forced him to go. Once outside the city, the people shot and killed him.

sentences.zh: 幽、安、營、並四州行台劉靈助，自謂方術可以動人，又推算知爾朱氏將衰，乃起兵自稱燕王、開府儀同三司、大行台，聲言為敬宗復仇，且妄述圖讖，云：「劉氏當王。

translations.literal: Liu Lingzhu, Grand Commissioner of the four provinces You, An, Ying, and Bing, believed his arts could move men. He also calculated by divination that the Erzhu clan would decline, and so raised troops, styling himself King of Yan, Bearer of the Staff with Equal Rank to the Three Dukes, and Grand Commissioner, proclaiming that he would avenge Jingzong and also falsely citing prophecies: "The Liu house shall be king."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lingzhu, Grand Commissioner of the four provinces You, An, Ying, and Bing, believed his arts could move men. He also calculated by divination that the Erzhu clan would decline, and so raised troops, styling himself King of Yan, Bearer of the Staff with Equal Rank to the Three Dukes, and Grand Commissioner, proclaiming that he would avenge Jingzong and also falsely citing prophecies: "The Liu house shall be king."

sentences.zh: 」由是幽、瀛、滄、冀之民多從之。

translations.literal: Because of this, many of the people of You, Ying, Cang, and Ji followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, many of the people of You, Ying, Cang, and Ji followed him.

sentences.zh: 從之者夜舉火為號，不舉火者諸村共屠之。

translations.literal: Followers raised torches by night as a signal; villages that did not raise torches were jointly slaughtered by the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Followers raised torches by night as a signal; villages that did not raise torches were jointly slaughtered by the rest.

sentences.zh: 引兵南至博陵之安國城。

translations.literal: He led his army south to Anguo city in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: He led his army south to Anguo city in Boling.

sentences.zh: 爾朱兆遣監軍孫白鷂至冀州，託言調發民馬，欲俟高乾兄弟送馬而收之。

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhao sent Military Supervisor Sun Baiyao to Jizhou, claiming to levy civilian horses, intending to seize the Gao brothers when they delivered the horses.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao sent Military Supervisor Sun Baiyao to Jizhou, claiming to levy civilian horses, intending to seize the Gao brothers when they delivered the horses.

sentences.zh: 乾等知之，與前河內太守封隆之等合謀，潛部勒壯士，襲據信都，殺白鷂，執刺史元嶷。

translations.literal: When Gan and the others learned of it, they joined former Henei Administrator Feng Longzhi and others in a secret plot, quietly mustering stalwarts, seizing Xindu by surprise, killing Baiyao, and taking Inspector Yuan Yi prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: When Gan and the others learned of it, they joined former Henei Administrator Feng Longzhi and others in a secret plot, quietly mustering stalwarts, seizing Xindu by surprise, killing Baiyao, and taking Inspector Yuan Yi prisoner.

sentences.zh: 乾等欲推其父翼行州事，翼曰：「和集鄉里，我不如封皮。

translations.literal: Gan and the others wished to push their father Yi to administer the province. Yi said, "In harmonizing the countryside I am not the equal of Feng Pi."
translations.idiomatic: Gan and the others wished to push their father Yi to administer the province. Yi said, "In harmonizing the countryside I am not the equal of Feng Pi."

sentences.zh: 」乃奉隆之行州事，為敬宗舉哀，將士皆縞素，升壇誓眾，移檄州郡，共討爾朱氏，仍受劉靈助節度。

translations.literal: They then installed Longzhi to run provincial affairs, mourned Jingzong, and all officers wore white. They ascended an altar to swear the host, circulated a proclamation through the commanderies, and together attacked the Erzhu clan, still accepting Liu Lingzhu's command.
translations.idiomatic: They then installed Longzhi to run provincial affairs, mourned Jingzong, and all officers wore white. They ascended an altar to swear the host, circulated a proclamation through the commanderies, and together attacked the Erzhu clan, still accepting Liu Lingzhu's command.

sentences.zh: 隆之，磨奴之族孫也。

translations.literal: Longzhi was a clansman of Monu, several generations removed.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhi was a clansman of Monu, several generations removed.

sentences.zh: 殷州刺史爾朱羽生將五千人襲信都，高敖曹不暇擐甲，將十餘騎馳擊之。

translations.literal: Yinzhou Inspector Erzhu Yusheng led five thousand men in a surprise attack on Xindu. Gao Aocao had no time to don armor; with a little more than ten horsemen he galloped to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Yinzhou Inspector Erzhu Yusheng led five thousand men in a surprise attack on Xindu. Gao Aocao had no time to don armor; with a little more than ten horsemen he galloped to strike them.

sentences.zh: 乾在城中繩下五百人，追救未及，敖曹已交兵，羽生敗走。

translations.literal: Gan, inside the city, lowered five hundred men on ropes. The rescue had not yet arrived when Aocao was already in battle. Yusheng was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Gan, inside the city, lowered five hundred men on ropes. The rescue had not yet arrived when Aocao was already in battle. Yusheng was defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 敖曹馬槊絕世，左右無不一當百，時人比之項籍。

translations.literal: Aocao's cavalry lance was unmatched in the age; none at his side failed to match a hundred. Men of the time compared him to Xiang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Aocao's cavalry lance was unmatched in the age; none at his side failed to match a hundred. Men of the time compared him to Xiang Yu.

sentences.zh: 高歡屯胡關大王山六旬，乃引兵東出，聲言討信都。

translations.literal: Gao Huan camped at Mount Dawang in Huguan for sixty days, then led his army east, proclaiming that he was going to attack Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan camped at Mount Dawang in Huguan for sixty days, then led his army east, proclaiming that he was going to attack Xindu.

sentences.zh: 信都人皆懼，高乾曰：「吾聞高晉州雄略蓋世，其志不居人下。

translations.literal: The people of Xindu were all afraid. Gao Gan said, "I have heard that Gao Jinzhou's bold strategy covers the age and that his ambition will not rest under another man.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Xindu were all afraid. Gao Gan said, "I have heard that Gao Jinzhou's bold strategy covers the age and that his ambition will not rest under another man.

sentences.zh: 且爾朱無道，弒君虐民，正是英雄立功之會，今日之來，必有深謀，吾當輕馬迎之，密參意旨，諸君勿懼也。

translations.literal: Moreover the Erzhu are without the Way, murdering the sovereign and tyrannizing the people—this is exactly the moment for a hero to win merit. Today's coming surely holds a deep design. I shall go to meet him lightly mounted and consult his intent in secret. Do not be afraid."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Erzhu are without the Way, murdering the sovereign and tyrannizing the people—this is exactly the moment for a hero to win merit. Today's coming surely holds a deep design. I shall go to meet him lightly mounted and consult his intent in secret. Do not be afraid."

sentences.zh: 」乃將十餘騎與封隆之子子繪潛謁歡於滏口，說歡曰：「爾朱酷逆，痛結人神，凡曰有知，莫不思奮。

translations.literal: He then took a little more than ten horsemen and, with Feng Longzhi's son Zihui, went in secret to call on Huan at Fekou and said to him, "The Erzhu are cruel and rebellious; grief binds gods and men together. All who have understanding long to rise.
translations.idiomatic: He then took a little more than ten horsemen and, with Feng Longzhi's son Zihui, went in secret to call on Huan at Fekou and said to him, "The Erzhu are cruel and rebellious; grief binds gods and men together. All who have understanding long to rise.

sentences.zh: 明公威德素著，天下傾心，若兵以義立，則屈強之徒不足為明公敵矣。

translations.literal: Your lordship's authority and virtue have long been established; the realm inclines its heart to you. If you raise arms in the name of righteousness, even the stubbornly strong will not be enough to be your enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Your lordship's authority and virtue have long been established; the realm inclines its heart to you. If you raise arms in the name of righteousness, even the stubbornly strong will not be enough to be your enemy."

sentences.zh: 鄙州雖小，戶口不減十萬，谷秸之稅，足濟軍資。

translations.literal: Though our province is small, its households are not fewer than a hundred thousand, and grain and straw taxes are enough to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Though our province is small, its households are not fewer than a hundred thousand, and grain and straw taxes are enough to supply the army.

sentences.zh: 願公熟思其計。

translations.literal: We beg your lordship to ponder the plan carefully."
translations.idiomatic: We beg your lordship to ponder the plan carefully."

sentences.zh: 」乾辭氣慷慨，歡大悅，與之同帳寢。

translations.literal: Gan spoke with fervor. Huan was greatly pleased and shared a tent with him to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Gan spoke with fervor. Huan was greatly pleased and shared a tent with him to sleep.

sentences.zh: 初，河南太守趙郡李顯甫，喜豪俠，集諸李數千家於殷州西山方五六十里居之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Xianfu, Administrator of Henan in Zhao commandery, loved bold fellowship and had gathered several thousand households of the Li clan on the western hills of Yinzhou over a stretch of fifty or sixty li.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Xianfu, Administrator of Henan in Zhao commandery, loved bold fellowship and had gathered several thousand households of the Li clan on the western hills of Yinzhou over a stretch of fifty or sixty li.

sentences.zh: 顯甫卒，子元忠繼之。

translations.literal: When Xianfu died, his son Yuanzhong succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianfu died, his son Yuanzhong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 家素富，多出貸求利，元忠悉焚契免責，鄉人甚敬之。

translations.literal: The family had long been wealthy and made many loans at interest. Yuanzhong burned all the contracts and released the debtors; the countryside greatly respected him.
translations.idiomatic: The family had long been wealthy and made many loans at interest. Yuanzhong burned all the contracts and released the debtors; the countryside greatly respected him.

sentences.zh: 時盜賊蜂起，清河有五百人西戍。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose everywhere. In Qinghe five hundred men went west on garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandits rose everywhere. In Qinghe five hundred men went west on garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 還，經趙郡，以路梗，共投元忠。

translations.literal: On their return they passed through Zhao commandery. The road was blocked, and they all threw themselves on Yuanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: On their return they passed through Zhao commandery. The road was blocked, and they all threw themselves on Yuanzhong.

sentences.zh: 元忠遣奴為導，曰：「若逢賊，但道李元忠遣。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong sent a slave as guide, saying, "If you meet bandits, only say that Li Yuanzhong sent you."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong sent a slave as guide, saying, "If you meet bandits, only say that Li Yuanzhong sent you."

sentences.zh: 」如言，賊皆捨避。

translations.literal: It was as he said; the bandits all let them pass.
translations.idiomatic: It was as he said; the bandits all let them pass.

sentences.zh: 及葛榮起，元忠帥宗黨作壘以自保，坐大槲樹下，前後斬違命者凡三百人。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong rose, Yuanzhong led his clan to build a stockade for self-defense. He sat under a great oak tree and in all beheaded three hundred who disobeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong rose, Yuanzhong led his clan to build a stockade for self-defense. He sat under a great oak tree and in all beheaded three hundred who disobeyed orders.

sentences.zh: 賊至，元忠輒擊卻之。

translations.literal: When bandits came, Yuanzhong always beat them back.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits came, Yuanzhong always beat them back.

sentences.zh: 葛榮曰：「我自中山至此，連為趙李所破，何以能成大事！

translations.literal: Ge Rong said, "From Zhongshan to here I have been broken again and again by the Zhao Li—how can I accomplish great things!"
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong said, "From Zhongshan to here I have been broken again and again by the Zhao Li—how can I accomplish great things!"

sentences.zh: 」乃悉眾攻圍，執元忠以隨軍。

translations.literal: He then led his full host to besiege and took Yuanzhong along with the army.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his full host to besiege and took Yuanzhong along with the army.

sentences.zh: 賊平，就拜南趙郡太守，好酒，無政績。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, Yuanzhong was appointed on the spot Administrator of Southern Zhao commandery. He loved wine and had no record of governance.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits were pacified, Yuanzhong was appointed on the spot Administrator of Southern Zhao commandery. He loved wine and had no record of governance.

sentences.zh: 及爾朱兆弒敬宗，元忠棄官歸，謀舉兵討之。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao murdered Jingzong, Yuanzhong left office and returned home, plotting to raise troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao murdered Jingzong, Yuanzhong left office and returned home, plotting to raise troops to attack him.

sentences.zh: 會高歡東出，元忠乘露車，載素箏濁酒以奉迎。

translations.literal: When Huan marched east, Yuanzhong rode an open cart carrying a plain zither and muddy wine to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan marched east, Yuanzhong rode an open cart carrying a plain zither and muddy wine to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 歡聞其酒客，未即見之。

translations.literal: Huan had heard he was a wine guest and did not see him at once.
translations.idiomatic: Huan had heard he was a wine guest and did not see him at once.

sentences.zh: 元忠下車獨坐，酌酒擘脯食之，謂門者曰：「本言公招延俊傑，今聞國士到門，不吐哺輟洗，其人可知，還吾刺，勿通也！

translations.literal: Yuanzhong got down from the cart and sat alone, poured wine, tore dried meat, and ate, and told the gatekeeper, "I was told your master summons outstanding men. Now I hear a man of the realm has come to the gate and will not spit out his food and pause his washing—you can tell what sort of man he is. Give back my card; do not announce me!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong got down from the cart and sat alone, poured wine, tore dried meat, and ate, and told the gatekeeper, "I was told your master summons outstanding men. Now I hear a man of the realm has come to the gate and will not spit out his food and pause his washing—you can tell what sort of man he is. Give back my card; do not announce me!"

sentences.zh: 」門者以告，歡遽見之，引入，觴再行，元忠車上取箏鼓之，長歌慷慨，歌闋，謂歡曰：「天下形勢可見，明公猶事爾朱邪？

translations.literal: The gatekeeper reported this. Huan hurried to see him, brought him in, and they exchanged cups twice. Yuanzhong took a zither from the cart and played; when the song ended he said to Huan, "The realm's situation can already be seen. Does your lordship still serve the Erzhu?"
translations.idiomatic: The gatekeeper reported this. Huan hurried to see him, brought him in, and they exchanged cups twice. Yuanzhong took a zither from the cart and played; when the song ended he said to Huan, "The realm's situation can already be seen. Does your lordship still serve the Erzhu?"

sentences.zh: 」歡曰：「富貴皆因彼所致，安敢不盡節！

translations.literal: Huan said, "Wealth and honor all come through them—how dare we not exhaust our loyalty!"
translations.idiomatic: Huan said, "Wealth and honor all come through them—how dare we not exhaust our loyalty!"

sentences.zh: 」元忠曰：「非英雄也！

translations.literal: Yuanzhong said, "Not a hero!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong said, "Not a hero!"

sentences.zh: 高乾邕兄弟來未？

translations.literal: Have the Gao brothers Gan and Yong come yet?"
translations.idiomatic: Have the Gao brothers Gan and Yong come yet?"

sentences.zh: 」時乾已見歡，歡紿之曰：「從叔輩粗，何肯來！

translations.literal: Gan had already seen Huan. Huan deceived him, saying, "Those uncles of mine are crude—how would they come!"
translations.idiomatic: Gan had already seen Huan. Huan deceived him, saying, "Those uncles of mine are crude—how would they come!"

sentences.zh: 」元忠曰：「雖粗，並解事。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong said, "Crude though they are, they both understand affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Crude though they are, they both understand affairs."

sentences.zh: 」歡曰：「趙郡醉矣。

translations.literal: " Huan said, "The Zhao commandery man is drunk."
translations.idiomatic: Huan said, "The man from Zhao commandery is drunk."

sentences.zh: 」使人扶出。

translations.literal: " He had someone support him out.
translations.idiomatic: He had someone help him out.

sentences.zh: 元忠不肯起，孫騰進曰：「此君天遣來，不可違也。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong would not rise. Sun Teng stepped forward and said, "This gentleman was sent by Heaven; he must not be turned away."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong refused to get up. Sun Teng stepped forward and said, "Heaven sent this man—you cannot turn him away."

sentences.zh: 」歡乃復留與語，元忠慷慨流涕，歡亦悲不自勝。

translations.literal: " Huan then kept him to talk again. Yuanzhong spoke passionately with tears streaming, and Huan too was overcome with grief.
translations.idiomatic: Huan kept him and talked on. Yuanzhong spoke with passionate tears; Huan too was overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 元忠因進策曰：「殷州小，無糧仗，不足以濟大事。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong thereupon offered a plan: "Yin Province is small, without grain or weapons, insufficient to accomplish a great undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong then offered counsel: "Yin Province is small—no grain, no arms, not enough to finish a great cause.

sentences.zh: 若向冀州，高乾邕兄弟必為明公主人，殷州便以賜委。

translations.literal: If you turn toward Ji Province, the brothers Gao Gan and Gao Yong will surely play host to you, my lord, and Yin Province may be given over to your disposal."
translations.idiomatic: Turn toward Ji Province and the brothers Gao Gan and Gao Yong will surely receive you as their lord; Yin Province you may grant as you please."

sentences.zh: 冀、殷既合，滄、瀛、幽、定自然弭服，唯劉誕黠胡或當乖拒，然非明公之敵。

translations.literal: Once Ji and Yin are united, Cang, Ying, You, and Ding will naturally submit. Only Liu Dan, a cunning barbarian, may defy you—yet he is no match for my lord."
translations.idiomatic: With Ji and Yin joined, Cang, Ying, You, and Ding will submit of themselves. Only Liu Dan, a sly barbarian, may resist—but he is no match for you."

sentences.zh: 」歡急握元忠手而謝焉。

translations.literal: " Huan hastily grasped Yuanzhong's hand and thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan seized Yuanzhong's hand and thanked him warmly.

sentences.zh: 歡至山東，約勒士卒，絲毫之物不聽侵犯，每過麥地，歡輒步牽馬。

translations.literal: When Huan reached Shandong, he disciplined his troops and forbade the slightest seizure; whenever he passed wheat fields, Huan would walk and lead his horse by hand.
translations.idiomatic: In Shandong Huan kept his men under strict discipline and allowed no pillaging; crossing wheat fields he always walked and led his horse by the bridle.

sentences.zh: 遠近聞之，皆稱高儀同將兵整肅，益歸心焉。

translations.literal: Near and far heard of this and all praised Commander Gao for keeping his troops in order, and hearts turned to him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Word spread near and far that Commander Gao's troops were disciplined, and loyalty to him deepened.

sentences.zh: 歡求糧於相州刺史劉誕，誕不與；

translations.literal: Huan sought grain from Xiangzhou inspector Liu Dan; Dan would not supply it.
translations.idiomatic: Huan asked Xiangzhou inspector Liu Dan for grain; Dan refused.

sentences.zh: 有車營租米，歡掠取之。

translations.literal: There was transport-camp rent grain; Huan seized it.
translations.idiomatic: There was rent grain from the transport camp; Huan took it by force.

sentences.zh: 進至信都，封隆之、高乾等開門納之。

translations.literal: Advancing to Xindu, Feng Longzhi, Gao Gan, and others opened the gates to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Xindu, where Feng Longzhi, Gao Gan, and others opened the gates and welcomed him in.

sentences.zh: 高敖曹時在外略地，聞之，以乾為婦人，遺以布裙。

translations.literal: Gao Aocao was then abroad raiding territory; hearing of this, he treated Gan as a woman and sent him a cloth skirt.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Aocao was out raiding at the time; when he heard, he mocked Gan as a woman and sent him a cloth skirt.

sentences.zh: 歡使世子澄以子孫禮見之，敖曹乃與俱來。

translations.literal: Huan had his heir Prince Cheng pay him a visit with the courtesy due a descendant, and Aocao then came along with him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan sent his heir Cheng to greet Aocao with the courtesy owed a junior kinsman, and Aocao then came in person.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，魏封長廣王曄為東海王，以青州刺史魯郡王肅為太師，淮陽王欣為太傅，爾朱世隆為太保，長孫稚為太尉，趙郡王諶為司空，徐州刺史爾朱仲遠、雍州刺史爾朱天光並為大將軍，并州刺史爾朱兆為天柱大將軍；

translations.literal: On guiyou, Wei enfeoffed Prince of Changgung Ye as Prince of Donghai, made Prince of Lu Commandery Su of Qing Province Grand Tutor, Prince of Huaiyang Xin Grand Preceptor, Erzhu Shilong Grand Guardian, Changsun Zhi Grand Marshal, Prince of Zhao Commandery Chen Minister of Works, Xuzhou inspector Erzhu Zhongyuan and Yongzhou inspector Erzhu Tianguang both Grand Generals, and Bingzhou inspector Erzhu Zhao Pillar of State Grand General;
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou Wei made Prince of Changgung Ye Prince of Donghai, Qingzhou's Prince of Lu Su Grand Tutor, Prince of Huaiyang Xin Grand Preceptor, Erzhu Shilong Grand Guardian, Changsun Zhi Grand Marshal, Prince of Zhao Chen Minister of Works, Xuzhou inspector Erzhu Zhongyuan and Yongzhou inspector Erzhu Tianguang each Grand General, and Bingzhou inspector Erzhu Zhao Pillar-of-State Grand General;

sentences.zh: 賜高歡爵勃海王，征使入朝。

translations.literal: Gao Huan was granted the title Prince of Bohai and summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was enfeoffed as Prince of Bohai and ordered to come to court.

sentences.zh: 長孫稚固辭太尉，乃以為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Changsun Zhi firmly declined Grand Marshal and was instead made General of Agile Cavalry and Bearer of the Staff with Equal Rank to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Zhi firmly declined Grand Marshal and was made General of Agile Cavalry with the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 爾朱兆辭天柱，曰：「此叔父所終之官，我何敢受！

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhao declined the Pillar of State, saying, "This was the office at which my uncle ended his life—how dare I accept it!"
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao declined the Pillar of State, saying, "My uncle died in that office—how dare I take it!"

sentences.zh: 」固辭，不拜，尋加都督十州諸軍事，世襲并州刺史。

translations.literal: " He firmly declined and did not accept, but was soon made Supervisor of Military Affairs for ten provinces with hereditary Bingzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the post, but was soon made commander of military affairs for ten provinces and hereditary Bingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 高歡辭不就征。

translations.literal: Gao Huan declined and did not answer the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan declined and did not go.

sentences.zh: 爾朱仲遠徙鎮大梁，復加兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhongyuan moved his headquarters to Daliang and was again made Yanzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhongyuan shifted his base to Daliang and was again named Yanzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 爾朱世隆之初為僕射也，畏爾朱榮之威嚴，深自刻厲，留心幾案，應接賓客，有開敏之名。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Shilong first became Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, he feared Erzhu Rong's stern authority, disciplined himself deeply, attended to his desk, received guests, and had a reputation for quick intelligence.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Shilong first became Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, he feared Rong's stern authority, kept himself rigorously in check, minded his desk, received guests courteously, and won a name for quick wit.

sentences.zh: 及榮死，無所顧憚，為尚書令，家居視事，坐符台省，事無大小，不先白世隆，有司不敢行。

translations.literal: After Rong died he had nothing to fear, became Director of the Masters of Writing, conducted business from home, sat at the Masters of Writing compound, and nothing great or small was done without first reporting to Shilong—the responsible offices dared not act.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong's death he feared nothing, took the post of Director of the Masters of Writing, ran affairs from home, and sat at the ministry compound; nothing large or small went forward without Shilong's word, and the offices dared not act on their own.

sentences.zh: 使尚書郎宋游道、邢昕在其聽事東西別坐，受納辭訟，稱命施行；

translations.literal: He had Masters of Writing Gentlemen Song Youdao and Xing Xin sit separately east and west in his reception hall to receive and decide lawsuits, issuing orders in his name;
translations.idiomatic: He set Masters of Writing Gentlemen Song Youdao and Xing Xin in his hall, east and west, to take suits and issue orders in his name;

sentences.zh: 公為貪淫，生殺自恣；

translations.literal: he was greedy and licentious and killed or spared at will;
translations.idiomatic: he was greedy and licentious and killed or spared as he pleased;

sentences.zh: 又欲收軍士之意，泛加階級，皆為將軍，無復員限，自是勳賞之官大致猥濫，人不復貴。

translations.literal: wishing also to win soldiers' hearts, he broadly raised ranks until all were generals with no limit on numbers—from then on merit titles were grossly debased and no longer esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: and to win the soldiers' favor he promoted everyone to general without limit, so that honors were debased and no longer prized.

sentences.zh: 是時，天光專制關右，兆奄有並、汾，仲遠擅命徐、兗，世隆居中用事，競為貪暴。

translations.literal: At this time Tianguang monopolized power west of the passes, Zhao held Bing and Fen, Zhongyuan gave orders at will in Xu and Yan, and Shilong wielded power at the center—all vied in greed and violence.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang ruled the west, Zhao held Bing and Fen, Zhongyuan did as he pleased in Xu and Yan, and Shilong ran the center—they all competed in greed and violence.

sentences.zh: 而仲遠尤甚，所部富室大族，多誣以謀反，籍沒其婦女財物入私家，投其男子於河，如是者不可勝數。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan was worst: in his territory he often accused wealthy great clans of treason, confiscated their women and goods for his private use, and threw the men into the river—such cases were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan was worst of all: he accused rich houses of rebellion, seized their women and goods for himself, and drowned the men in the river—beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 自滎陽已東，租稅悉入其軍，不送洛陽。

translations.literal: From Xingyang eastward all taxes went to his army and were not sent to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: East of Xingyang all taxes went to his army, not to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 東南州郡自牧守以下至士民，畏仲遠如豺狼。

translations.literal: In the southeastern provinces, from governors and prefects down to commoners, all feared Zhongyuan as they would wolves.
translations.idiomatic: From governors down to commoners in the southeast, all feared Zhongyuan like wolves.

sentences.zh: 由是四方之人皆惡爾朱氏，而憚其強，莫敢違也。

translations.literal: Thus people everywhere hated the Erzhu clan yet feared their strength and none dared defy them.
translations.idiomatic: So the realm hated the Erzhu, yet feared their power and none dared resist.

sentences.zh: 己丑，魏以涇州刺史賀拔岳為岐州刺史，渭州刺史侯莫陳悅為秦州刺史，並加儀同三司。

translations.literal: On jichou Wei made Jingzhou inspector Heba Yue Jizhou inspector and Weizhou inspector Houmochen Yue Qinzhou inspector, both with the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Wei made Jingzhou inspector Heba Yue inspector of Qi and Weizhou inspector Houmochen Yue inspector of Qin, each with the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 魏使大都督侯淵、驃騎大將軍代人叱列延慶討劉靈助，至固城，淵畏其眾，欲引兵西入，據關拒險，以待其變。

translations.literal: Wei sent Grand Commander Hou Yuan and General of Agile Cavalry Chilie Yanqing, a man of Dai, to attack Liu Lingzhu. Reaching Gucheng, Yuan feared their numbers and wished to withdraw west, hold the passes, and wait for change.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent Grand Commander Hou Yuan and General of Agile Cavalry Chilie Yanqing of Dai against Liu Lingzhu. At Gucheng Yuan feared their numbers and wanted to pull west, hold the passes, and wait.

sentences.zh: 延慶曰：「靈助庸人，假妖術以惑眾。

translations.literal: Yanqing said, "Lingzhu is a mediocrity who uses sorcery to delude the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing said, "Lingzhu is a nobody who fools the crowd with sorcery.

sentences.zh: 大兵一臨，彼皆恃其符厭，豈肯戮力致死，與吾爭勝負哉！

translations.literal: When great troops arrive they will all rely on their charms—how would they fight to the death and contend with us for victory!"
translations.idiomatic: When the army comes they will trust their charms—who will fight to the death against us?"

sentences.zh: 不如出營城外，詐言西歸。

translations.literal: Better to leave camp outside the walls and falsely announce a return west.
translations.idiomatic: Better leave camp outside the walls and pretend we are marching west.

sentences.zh: 靈助聞之，必自寬縱，然後潛軍擊之，往則成擒矣。

translations.literal: When Lingzhu hears this he will surely relax; then strike secretly and you will take him at once."
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhu will relax; then strike by night and he is yours at once."

sentences.zh: 」淵從之，出頓城西，聲雲欲還，丙申，簡精騎一千夜發，直抵靈助壘；

translations.literal: " Yuan followed this, encamped west of the city, and announced he would return. On bingshen he chose a thousand elite horsemen, set out by night, and went straight to Lingzhu's camp;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan agreed, camped west of the city, and said he would withdraw. On bingshen he took a thousand picked horsemen, rode by night, and struck Lingzhu's camp;

sentences.zh: 靈助戰敗，斬之，傳首洛陽。

translations.literal: Lingzhu was defeated and beheaded, and his head was sent to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhu was defeated and killed; his head was sent to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 初，靈助起兵，自佔勝負，曰：「三月之末，我必入定州，爾朱氏不久當滅。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Lingzhu raised troops, he divined his own fortune and said, "At the end of the third month I shall enter Ding Province; the Erzhu will soon be destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: When Lingzhu rose he divined and said, "At month's end in the third month I enter Ding Province; the Erzhu will soon fall."

sentences.zh: 」及靈助首函入定州，果以是月之末。

translations.literal: " When Lingzhu's head in its box reached Ding Province, it was indeed at that month's end.
translations.idiomatic: When his head in a box reached Ding Province, it was indeed at that month's end.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙巳，昭明太子統卒。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on yisi, Crown Prince Zhaoming Tong died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on yisi, Crown Prince Zhaoming Tong died.

sentences.zh: 太子自加元服，上即使省錄朝政，百司進事，填委於前，太子辨析詐謬，秋毫必睹，但令改正，不加案劾，平斷法獄，多所全宥，寬和容眾，喜慍不形於色。

translations.literal: Since the crown prince had come of age the emperor had him review and record court affairs; matters from all offices piled before him, and the prince distinguished fraud from truth, seeing the slightest error, only ordering correction without prosecuting, judging law cases fairly and sparing many, gentle and tolerant, never showing anger or pleasure on his face.
translations.idiomatic: After his capping the emperor had him oversee court business; papers from every office piled up, yet he spotted every error, ordered correction without prosecution, judged cases leniently, and was gentle and even-tempered.

sentences.zh: 好讀書屬文，引接才俊，賞愛無倦。

translations.literal: He loved reading and composition, welcomed men of talent, and never tired of rewarding them.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books and writing, welcomed talent, and never wearied of encouraging them.

sentences.zh: 出宮二十餘年，不畜聲樂。

translations.literal: For more than twenty years outside the palace he kept no music.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years out of the palace he kept no musicians.

sentences.zh: 每霖雨積雪，遣左右周行閭巷，視貧者賑之。

translations.literal: Whenever rain or snow lasted long he sent attendants through the lanes to find the poor and relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: In long rains or snow he sent men through the lanes to aid the poor.

sentences.zh: 天性孝謹，在東宮，雖燕居，坐起恆西向，或宿被召當入，危坐達旦。

translations.literal: By nature filial and careful, in the Eastern Palace even at ease he always faced west when sitting or rising; if summoned at night to enter, he would sit upright until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Filial by nature, in the Eastern Palace he always faced west even at rest; if called at night he sat upright until dawn.

sentences.zh: 及寢疾，恐貽帝憂，敕參問，輒自力手書。

translations.literal: When ill he feared troubling the emperor and ordered that inquiries be answered in his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: In illness, lest he worry the emperor, he answered every inquiry in his own hand.

sentences.zh: 及卒，朝野惋愕，建康男女，奔走宮門，號泣滿路。

translations.literal: At his death court and country were stunned; men and women of Jiankang ran to the palace gates and wept along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: At his death court and country mourned; men and women of Jiankang filled the streets with weeping.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，魏以高歡為大都督、東道大行台、冀州刺史，又以安定王爾朱智虎為肆州刺史。

translations.literal: On guichou Wei made Gao Huan Grand Commander, Eastern Route Grand Commissioner, and Jizhou inspector, and made Prince of Anding Erzhu Zhihu Sizhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Wei made Gao Huan Grand Commander, Eastern Route Grand Commissioner, and Jizhou inspector, and Prince of Anding Erzhu Zhihu Sizhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 魏爾朱天光出夏州，遣將討宿勤明達，癸亥，擒明達，送洛陽，斬之。

translations.literal: Wei's Erzhu Tianguang left Xia Province and sent generals against Suqin Mingda; on guihai Mingda was captured, sent to Luoyang, and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Tianguang left Xia Province, sent generals against Suqin Mingda, and on guihai captured him, sent him to Luoyang, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，魏以侍中、驃騎大將軍爾朱彥伯為司徒。

translations.literal: On bingyin Wei made Palace Attendant and General of Agile Cavalry Erzhu Yanbo Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Wei made Palace Attendant and General of Agile Cavalry Erzhu Yanbo Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 魏詔有司不得復稱「偽梁」。

translations.literal: Wei ordered that the authorities must no longer say "false Liang."
translations.idiomatic: Wei ordered officials to stop calling Liang "the false Liang."

sentences.zh: 五月，丙子，魏荊州城民斬趙修延，復推李琰之行州事。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on bingzi, the people of Jingzhou city killed Zhao Xiuyan and again made Li Yan'an act as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on bingzi, Jingzhou townspeople killed Zhao Xiuyan and again put Li Yan'an in charge.

sentences.zh: 魏爾朱仲遠使都督魏僧勖等討崔祖螭於東陽，斬之。

translations.literal: Wei's Erzhu Zhongyuan sent Commander Wei Sengqin and others against Cui Zuci at Dongyang and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhongyuan sent Commander Wei Sengqin against Cui Zuci at Dongyang and killed him.

sentences.zh: 初，昭明太子葬其母丁貴嬪，遣人求墓地之吉者。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Crown Prince Zhaoming buried his mother Lady Ding the Noble Consort, he sent men to seek an auspicious grave site.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Zhaoming buried his mother Lady Ding, he sent men to find an auspicious tomb site.

sentences.zh: 或賂宦者俞三副求賣地，雲若得錢三百萬，以百萬與之。

translations.literal: Some bribed the eunuch Yu Sanfu to sell a plot, saying that if they got three million cash, one million would go to him.
translations.idiomatic: Some bribed the eunuch Yu Sanfu to sell a plot, promising him a million of three million cash.

sentences.zh: 三副密啟上，言「太子所得地，不如今地於上為吉」。

translations.literal: Sanfu secretly reported to the emperor, "The site the prince obtained is not as auspicious for Your Majesty as this one."
translations.idiomatic: Sanfu secretly told the emperor, "The prince's site is not as lucky for Your Majesty as this one."

sentences.zh: 上年老多忌，即命市之。

translations.literal: The emperor, old and full of taboos, at once ordered it bought.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, old and superstitious, at once bought it.

sentences.zh: 葬畢，有道士云：「此地不利長子，若厭之，或可申延。

translations.literal: After the burial a Daoist said, "This ground is ill for the eldest son; if you perform a suppression rite, his life may be extended."
translations.idiomatic: After burial a Daoist said, "This ground harms the eldest son; a suppression rite might extend his life."

sentences.zh: 」乃為蠟鵝及諸物埋於墓側長子位。

translations.literal: " So wax geese and other objects were buried beside the tomb in the eldest son's place.
translations.idiomatic: Wax geese and other objects were buried at the eldest son's place beside the tomb.

sentences.zh: 宮監鮑邈之、魏雅初皆有寵於太子，邈之晚見疏於雅，乃密啟上云：「雅為太子厭禱。

translations.literal: Palace supervisor Bao Miaozhi and Wei Ya had once been favored by the prince; Miaozhi later lost favor to Ya and secretly reported to the emperor, "Ya performed curse-rites against the prince for the crown prince."
translations.idiomatic: Palace supervisors Bao Miaozhi and Wei Ya had once been favored by the prince; Miaozhi, later eclipsed by Ya, secretly told the emperor Ya had cursed the prince on the crown prince's behalf.

sentences.zh: 」上遣檢掘，果得鵝物，大驚，將窮其事。

translations.literal: " The emperor sent men to dig and indeed found the goose objects; he was greatly alarmed and was about to pursue the matter to the end.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the site dug up and found the objects; greatly alarmed, he was about to investigate fully.

sentences.zh: 徐勉固諫而止，但誅道士。

translations.literal: Xu Mian firmly remonstrated and stopped him; only the Daoist was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mian remonstrated firmly and stopped him; only the Daoist was executed.

sentences.zh: 由是太子終身慚憤，不能自明。

translations.literal: From this the prince bore shame and anger all his life and could never clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: The prince lived on in shame and anger and could never clear his name.

sentences.zh: 及卒，上征其長子南徐州刺史華容公歡至建康，欲立以為嗣，銜其前事，猶豫久之，卒不立，庚寅，遣還鎮。

translations.literal: At his death the emperor summoned his eldest son, Southern Xuzhou inspector Prince of Huarong Huan, to Jiankang, wishing to make him heir; brooding on the earlier affair, he hesitated long and in the end did not establish him. On gengyin he sent him back to his post.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the emperor summoned his eldest son Huan, Prince of Huarong and Southern Xuzhou inspector, intending to make him heir; brooding on the old affair, he hesitated long, did not establish him, and on gengyin sent him back.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：君子之於正道，不可少頃離也，不可跬步失也。

translations.literal: Master Guang says: In the correct Way a gentleman may not leave it for an instant or lose it in a single step.
translations.idiomatic: Master Guang remarks: A gentleman may not leave the right Way for an instant or miss it in a single step.

sentences.zh: 以昭明太子之仁孝，武帝之慈愛，一染嫌疑之跡，身以憂死，罪及後昆，求吉得凶，不可湔滌，可不戒哉！

translations.literal: With Crown Prince Zhaoming's benevolence and filial piety and Emperor Wu's affection, one stain of suspicion cost him his life in grief, brought guilt on his descendants, sought good and found ill—what cannot be washed away! Therefore the devious and the strange arts are what gentlemen keep far from.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoming's benevolence and Wu's love—and one shadow of suspicion cost the prince his life, harmed his sons, turned good omens to ill: a stain that cannot be washed away. Hence devious men and strange arts are what gentlemen shun.

sentences.zh: 是以詭誕之士，奇邪之術，君子遠之。

translations.literal: On bingshen Prince of Jin'an Gang was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Prince of Jin'an Gang was made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 丙申，立太子母弟晉安王綱為皇太子。

translations.literal: Court and country mostly thought it wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country mostly thought it wrong.

sentences.zh: 朝野多以為不順，司議侍郎周弘正，嘗為晉安王主簿，乃奏記曰：「謙讓道廢，多歷年所。

translations.literal: Reviewing Secretary Zhou Hongzheng, who had once been Prince of Jin'an's chief clerk, submitted a memorial saying, "The way of yielding has been in ruins for many years.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing Secretary Zhou Hongzheng, once the prince's chief clerk, memorialized: "The way of yielding has lain in ruins for years.

sentences.zh: 伏惟明大王殿下，天挺將聖，四海歸仁，是以皇上發德音，以大王為儲副。

translations.literal: I consider that Your Highness the Prince of Jin'an, Heaven-sent to sagehood, all within the seas turns to your benevolence; therefore the emperor issued a virtuous decree making Your Highness heir.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness is Heaven's chosen sage; the realm turns to you; the emperor has named you heir.

sentences.zh: 意者願聞殿下抗目夷上仁之義，執子臧大賢之節，逃玉輿而弗乘，棄萬乘如脫屣，庶改澆競之俗，以大吳國之風。

translations.literal: I venture to hope Your Highness will lift your eyes to the benevolence of Yi the Archer, hold to Prince Zang's great worth, flee the jade chariot and not ride it, cast off the ten thousand chariots as one casts off shoes—perhaps to change the custom of strife and enlarge the wind of great Wu.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Highness to look to Yi's yielding, hold to Prince Zang's refusal, leave the chariot unmounted, cast off the realm like old shoes—perhaps to change our strife and revive great Wu's virtue.

sentences.zh: 古有其人，今聞其語，能行之者，非殿下而誰！

translations.literal: The ancients had such men; today we hear such words; who but Your Highness can do it!
translations.idiomatic: The ancients did this; today we hear the words—who but Your Highness can act on them!

sentences.zh: 使無為之化復生於遂古，讓王之道不墜於來葉，豈不盛歟！

translations.literal: Let the rule of non-action live again in remote antiquity and the way of the yielding king not fall in later ages—would it not be glorious!"
translations.idiomatic: Let non-action rule again and the yielding king's way stand in later ages—would it not be glorious!"

sentences.zh: 」王不能從。

translations.literal: " The prince could not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: The prince would not listen.

sentences.zh: 弘正，捨之兄子也。

translations.literal: Hongzheng was a nephew of She.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng was She's nephew.

sentences.zh: 太子以侍讀東海徐摛為家令，兼管記，尋帶領直。

translations.literal: The crown prince made Donghai Xu Chi household steward, also in charge of records, and soon head of the crown prince's guard.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince made Xu Chi of Donghai household steward and recorder, soon head of the crown prince's guard.

sentences.zh: 摛文體輕麗，春坊盡學之，時人謂之宮體。

translations.literal: Chi's style was light and elegant; the Eastern Palace all imitated it, and people of the time called it Palace Style.
translations.idiomatic: Chi wrote in a light, elegant style; the Eastern Palace imitated him, and men called it Palace Style.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，怒，召摛，欲加誚責。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of this, grew angry, and summoned Chi to rebuke him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard, grew angry, and summoned Chi to rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 及見，應對明敏，辭義可觀，意更釋然。

translations.literal: When he saw him, Chi answered clearly and his words were worth seeing; the emperor's mind eased.
translations.idiomatic: Face to face Chi was quick and clear; the emperor's anger faded.

sentences.zh: 因問經史及釋教，摛商較從橫，應對如響，上甚加歎異，寵遇日隆。

translations.literal: He asked about the classics, histories, and Buddhism; Chi compared and debated freely and answered like an echo; the emperor marveled and favored him more day by day.
translations.idiomatic: He questioned him on classics, histories, and Buddhism; Chi debated freely and answered like an echo; the emperor marveled and favored him daily.

sentences.zh: 領軍朱異不悅，謂所親曰：「徐叟出入兩宮，漸來見逼，我須早為之所。

translations.literal: Commander of the Guards Zhu Yi was displeased and said to those close to him, "Old Xu goes in and out of both palaces and presses on me—I must act early."
translations.idiomatic: Commander of the Guards Zhu Yi was displeased and said, "Old Xu haunts both palaces and crowds me—I must move first."

sentences.zh: 」遂乘間白上曰：「摛年老，又愛泉石，意在一郡自養。

translations.literal: " He then took occasion to tell the emperor, "Chi is old and loves springs and rocks; his wish is to nourish himself in one commandery."
translations.idiomatic: He told the emperor, "Chi is old and loves landscape; he wishes to retire to a commandery."

sentences.zh: 」上謂摛真欲之，乃召摛，謂曰：「新安大好山水。

translations.literal: " The emperor thought Chi truly wished it and summoned him, saying, "Xin'an has fine mountains and waters."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought Chi meant it, summoned him, and said, "Xin'an has fine mountains and waters."

sentences.zh: 」遂出為新安太守。

translations.literal: " He was then sent out as Xin'an prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Chi was sent out as prefect of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸丑，立華容公歡為豫章王，其弟枝江公譽為河東王，曲阿公QKDP為岳陽王。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on guichou, Prince of Huarong Huan was made Prince of Yuzhang, his brother Prince of Zhijiang Yu Prince of Hedong, and Prince of Qu'e Cha Prince of Yueyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on guichou, Prince of Huarong Huan was made Prince of Yuzhang, Prince of Zhijiang Yu Prince of Hedong, and Prince of Qu'e Cha Prince of Yueyang.

sentences.zh: 上以人言不息，故封歡兄弟以大郡，用慰其心。

translations.literal: Because talk did not cease, the emperor enfeoffed Huan's brothers with large commanderies to comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Because rumors would not die down, the emperor enfeoffed Huan's brothers in large commanderies to comfort them.

sentences.zh: 久之，鮑邈之坐誘略人，罪不至死，太子綱追思昭明之冤，揮淚誅之。

translations.literal: Long afterward Bao Miaozhi was charged with enticement; the crime did not merit death, but Crown Prince Gang, recalling Zhaoming's wrong, wept as he had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Long after, Bao Miaozhi was charged with enticement—a capital crime by law, but Crown Prince Gang, remembering Zhaoming's wrong, wept as he had him executed.

sentences.zh: 魏高歡將起兵討爾朱氏，鎮南大將軍斛律金、軍主善無庫狄千與歡妻弟婁昭、妻之姊夫段榮皆勸成之。

translations.literal: Wei's Gao Huan was about to raise troops against the Erzhu. Grand General Who Guards the South Hulu Jin, army commander Shanwu Kudigan Qian, Huan's wife's brother Lou Zhao, and his wife's brother-in-law Duan Rong all urged him to it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was about to rise against the Erzhu; Grand General Who Guards the South Hulu Jin, army commander Kudigan Qian of Shanwu, his wife's brother Lou Zhao, and his wife's brother-in-law Duan Rong all urged him on.

sentences.zh: 歡乃詐為書，稱爾朱兆將以六鎮人配契胡為部曲，眾皆憂懼。

translations.literal: Huan then forged a letter saying Erzhu Zhao would assign the Six Garrisons men to Qi Hu households as retainers, and all were fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Huan forged a letter saying Erzhu Zhao would assign Six Garrisons men to Qi Hu households as retainers, and all were afraid.

sentences.zh: 又為并州符，徵兵討步落稽，發萬人，將遣之。

translations.literal: He also forged a Bingzhou dispatch to levy troops against the Buluoji, mustered ten thousand men, and was about to send them.
translations.idiomatic: He forged a Bingzhou order to levy troops against the Buluoji, raised ten thousand men, and prepared to send them.

sentences.zh: 孫騰與都督尉景為請留五日，如此者再，歡親送之郊，雪涕執別，眾皆號慟，聲震郊野。

translations.literal: Sun Teng and Commander Wei Jing asked leave of five days for them—twice thus—and Huan personally saw them off in the suburbs, weeping as he took leave; all wailed until the countryside shook.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng and Commander Wei Jing twice asked five days' delay; Huan saw them off in the suburbs with tears; the men wailed till the fields shook.

sentences.zh: 歡乃諭之曰：「與爾俱為失鄉客，義同一家，不意在上征發乃爾！

translations.literal: Huan then addressed them: "I am with you all fellow exiles from home, one family in spirit—who thought the court would levy us so!"
translations.idiomatic: Huan told them, "We are exiles together, one family—who thought the court would press us so!"

sentences.zh: 今直西向，已當死，後軍期，又當死，配國人，又當死，奈何？

translations.literal: Go straight west and you die; miss the army deadline and you die; be assigned to native households and you die—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: March west and you die; miss the deadline and you die; be assigned to native households and you die—what then?"

sentences.zh: 」眾曰：「唯有反耳！

translations.literal: " The crowd said, "Only rebellion!"
translations.idiomatic: They cried, "Only rebellion!"

sentences.zh: 」歡曰：「反乃急計，然當推一人為主，誰可者？

translations.literal: " Huan said, "Rebellion is an urgent plan, yet we must choose one man as leader—who will do?"
translations.idiomatic: Huan said, "Rebellion is urgent—but we need a leader. Who?"

sentences.zh: 」眾共推歡，歡曰：「爾鄉里難制。

translations.literal: " All together pushed Huan. Huan said, "Your fellow townsmen are hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: All pushed Huan. Huan said, "Your townsmen are hard to rule.

sentences.zh: 不見葛榮乎？

translations.literal: Have you not seen Ge Rong?
translations.idiomatic: Have you not seen Ge Rong?

sentences.zh: 雖有百萬之眾，曾無法度，終自敗滅。

translations.literal: Although he had a million followers, he had no discipline and was destroyed in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Though he commanded a million men, he had no discipline and destroyed himself in the end.

sentences.zh: 今以吾為主，當與前異，毋得陵漢人，犯軍令，生死任吾則可；

translations.literal: Now with me as your leader, things must differ from before: you must not bully Han Chinese or break army law—if you leave life and death to me, it can be done;
translations.idiomatic: Now you make me leader—we do things differently: no bullying Han Chinese, no breaking army law; leave life and death to me, and it can be done;

sentences.zh: 不然，不能為天下笑。

translations.literal: otherwise you will only make the world laugh.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise the world will only laugh at us.

sentences.zh: 」眾皆頓顙曰：「死生唯命！

translations.literal: " All kowtowed and said, "Life and death are yours to command!"
translations.idiomatic: All kowtowed: "Life and death—we obey!"

sentences.zh: 」歡乃椎牛饗士，庚申，起兵於信都，亦未敢顯言叛爾朱氏也。

translations.literal: " Huan then slaughtered oxen to feast the soldiers. On gengshen he raised troops at Xindu, still not daring openly to say he rebelled against the Erzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Huan feasted the troops with slaughtered oxen. On gengshen he rose at Xindu, still not daring to declare rebellion against the Erzhu openly.

sentences.zh: 會李元忠舉兵逼殷州，歡令高乾帥眾救之。

translations.literal: When Li Yuanzhong raised troops and pressed Yin Province, Huan ordered Gao Gan to lead men to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanzhong pressed Yin Province; Huan sent Gao Gan to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 乾輕騎入見刺史爾朱羽生，與指畫軍計，羽生與乾俱出，因擒斬之，持羽生首謁歡。

translations.literal: Gan went in with light cavalry to see inspector Erzhu Yusheng, discussed military plans with him, and when Yusheng came out with Gan he was seized and beheaded; Gan brought Yusheng's head to pay court to Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Gan rode in lightly to see inspector Erzhu Yusheng, laid out the plan, and when Yusheng came out with him seized and beheaded him, then brought the head to Huan.

sentences.zh: 歡撫膺曰：「今日反決矣！

translations.literal: Huan clutched his breast and said, "Today rebellion is settled!"
translations.idiomatic: Huan struck his breast: "Today the revolt is decided!"

sentences.zh: 」乃以元忠為殷州刺史，鎮廣阿。

translations.literal: " He then made Yuanzhong Yin Province inspector, garrisoned at Guang'a.
translations.idiomatic: He made Yuanzhong Yin Province inspector at Guang'a.

sentences.zh: 歡於是抗表罪狀爾朱氏，爾朱世隆匿之不通。

translations.literal: Huan thereupon submitted a memorial listing the Erzhu clan's crimes; Erzhu Shilong hid it and would not pass it on.
translations.idiomatic: Huan memorialized the Erzhu crimes; Shilong suppressed the memorial.

sentences.zh: 魏楊播及弟椿、津皆有名德。

translations.literal: Wei's Yang Bo and his younger brothers Chun and Jin all had famous virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei, Yang Bo and his brothers Chun and Jin were men of famed virtue.

sentences.zh: 播剛毅，椿、津謙恭，家世孝友，緦服同爨，男女百口，人無間言。

translations.literal: Bo was firm and resolute; Chun and Jin humble and respectful. Their house was filial and friendly for generations, mourning garb and cooking together, a hundred mouths male and female, and no one spoke against them.
translations.idiomatic: Bo was stern; Chun and Jin modest. For generations the family lived in filial harmony, a hundred kin under one roof, without reproach.

sentences.zh: 椿、津皆至三公，一門七郡太守，三十二州刺史。

translations.literal: Chun and Jin both reached the Three Dukes; one household produced seven commandery governors and thirty-two provincial inspectors.
translations.idiomatic: Chun and Jin both reached the Three Dukes; one clan held seven prefectures and thirty-two provinces.

sentences.zh: 敬宗之誅爾朱榮也，播子侃預其謀；

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingzong killed Erzhu Rong, Bo's son Kan took part in the plot;
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzong killed Erzhu Rong, Bo's son Kan joined the plot;

sentences.zh: 城陽王徽、李彧，皆其姻戚也。

translations.literal: Prince of Chengyang Hui and Li Yu were both their kin by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Chengyang Hui and Li Yu were both their in-laws.

sentences.zh: 爾朱兆入洛，侃逃歸華陰，爾朱天光使侃婦父韋義遠招之，與盟，許貰其罪。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Kan fled to Huayin. Erzhu Tianguang had Kan's father-in-law Wei Yiyuan summon him, made an alliance, and promised to spare his crime.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao entered Luoyang, Kan fled to Huayin. Tianguang had his father-in-law Wei Yiyuan summon him, allied with him, and promised pardon.

sentences.zh: 侃曰：「彼雖食言，死者不過一人，猶冀全百口。

translations.literal: Kan said, "Though they break faith, only one man dies; I still hope to save the hundred mouths."
translations.idiomatic: Kan said, "If they break faith, only I die—I may yet save the clan."

sentences.zh: 」乃出應之，天光殺之。

translations.literal: " He then came out in answer and Tianguang killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He came out; Tianguang killed him.

sentences.zh: 時椿致仕，與其子昱在華陰，椿弟冀州刺史順、司空津、順子東雍州刺史辨、正平太守仲宣皆在洛。

translations.literal: At the time Chun had retired and was with his son Yu at Huayin; Chun's younger brother Jizhou inspector Shun, Minister of Works Jin, Shun's son Eastern Yongzhou inspector Bian, and Zhengping prefect Zhongxuan were all in Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Chun had retired and was with his son Yu at Huayin; brother Shun was Jizhou inspector, Jin was Minister of Works, and Shun's sons Bian and Zhongxuan held posts in the east and at Luo.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，爾朱世隆誣奏楊氏謀反，請收治之，魏主不許。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Erzhu Shilong falsely memorialized that the Yang clan plotted rebellion and asked to arrest them; the Wei emperor refused.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Shilong accused the Yangs of treason and asked to arrest them; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 世隆苦請，帝不得已，命有司檢案以聞。

translations.literal: Shilong pressed hard; the emperor had no choice and ordered the authorities to investigate and report.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong pressed until the emperor ordered an investigation.

sentences.zh: 壬申夜，世隆遣兵圍津第，天光亦遣兵掩椿家於華陰。

translations.literal: On renshen night Shilong sent troops to surround Jin's residence, and Tianguang sent troops to strike Chun's house at Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen night Shilong besieged Jin's house and Tianguang raided Chun at Huayin.

sentences.zh: 東西之族無少長皆殺之，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: East and west, none young or old was spared; their households were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: East and west, young and old were killed; their property was seized.

sentences.zh: 世隆奏云：「楊氏實反，與收兵相拒，皆已格殺。

translations.literal: Shilong memorialized, "The Yang clan truly rebelled and resisted arrest with arms—all have been killed in the fray."
translations.idiomatic: Shilong reported the Yangs had rebelled and been killed resisting arrest.

sentences.zh: 」帝惋悵久之，不言而已，朝野聞之，無不痛憤。

translations.literal: The emperor grieved long and said nothing; court and country heard and none did not feel pain and rage.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved in silence; court and country burned with outrage.

sentences.zh: 津子逸為光州刺史，爾朱仲遠遣使就殺之。

translations.literal: Jin's son Yi was Guangzhou inspector; Erzhu Zhongyuan sent men to kill him on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's son Yi, Guangzhou inspector, was killed on Zhongyuan's order.

sentences.zh: 唯津子愔於被收時適出在外，逃匿，獲免，往見高歡於信都，泣訴家禍，因為言討爾朱氏之策。

translations.literal: Only Jin's son Yin, having gone out when the arrest came, escaped and survived; he went to see Gao Huan at Xindu, wept over his family's disaster, and spoke of a plan to attack the Erzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yin, out when the arrest came, escaped; he came to Huan at Xindu, wept over the slaughter, and urged war on the Erzhu.

sentences.zh: 歡甚重之，即署行台郎中。

translations.literal: Huan valued him greatly and at once made him Eastern Route Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Huan esteemed him and made him Eastern Route Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，上臨軒策拜太子，大赦。

translations.literal: On yihai the emperor faced the hall to invest the crown prince and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the emperor invested the crown prince and proclaimed amnesty.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，魏司徒爾朱彥伯以旱遜位。

translations.literal: On bingxu Wei Minister of Works Erzhu Yanbo resigned on account of drought.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Erzhu Yanbo resigned as Minister of Works because of drought.

sentences.zh: 戊子，以彥伯為侍中、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On wuzi Yanbo was made Palace Attendant and Bearer of the Staff with Equal Rank to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Yanbo became Palace Attendant with the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 彥伯于兄弟中差無過惡。

translations.literal: Among the brothers Yanbo was comparatively without great crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Of the brothers Yanbo was the least guilty.

sentences.zh: 爾朱世隆固讓太保，魏主特置儀同三師之官，位次上公之下，庚寅，以世隆為之。

translations.literal: Erzhu Shilong firmly declined Grand Guardian; the Wei emperor specially created the office of Mentor with Staff Equal to the Three Masters, ranking below the Three Dukes. On gengyin Shilong was made to it.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong declined Grand Guardian; the court created Mentors with Staff below the Three Dukes, and on gengyin Shilong took that post.

sentences.zh: 斛斯椿譖朱瑞於世隆，世隆殺之。

translations.literal: Husi Chun slandered Zhu Rui to Shilong, and Shilong killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Husi Chun slandered Zhu Rui; Shilong had him killed.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，詔：「凡宗戚有服屬者，並可賜沐，食鄉亭侯，隨遠近為差。

translations.literal: On gengyin an edict said, "All kinsmen within the mourning grades may receive stipends, eating as district marquises, with differences according to distance."
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin an edict granted stipends to kinsmen within mourning grades, as district marquises by degree of kinship.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以吏部尚書何敬容為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On renchen Minister of the Civil Service He Rongrong was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen He Rongrong became Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 敬容，昌宇之子也。

translations.literal: Rongrong was a son of Changyu.
translations.idiomatic: Rongrong was Changyu's son.

sentences.zh: 魏爾朱仲遠、度律等聞高歡起兵，恃其強，不以為慮，獨爾朱世隆憂之。

translations.literal: Wei's Erzhu Zhongyuan, Dulu, and others heard Gao Huan had raised troops and, trusting their strength, did not take it seriously—only Erzhu Shilong was worried.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhongyuan, Dulu, and others heard Huan had risen and, trusting their strength, scorned him—only Shilong was afraid.

sentences.zh: 爾朱兆將步騎二萬出井陘，趣殷州，李元忠棄城奔信都。

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhao was about to lead twenty thousand infantry and cavalry out of Jingxing toward Yin Province; Li Yuanzhong abandoned the city and fled to Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao led twenty thousand out of Jingxing toward Yin; Yuanzhong abandoned the city and fled to Xindu.

sentences.zh: 八月，丙午，爾朱仲遠、度律將兵討高歡。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on bingwu, Erzhu Zhongyuan and Dulu led troops against Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu in the eighth month Zhongyuan and Dulu marched against Huan.

sentences.zh: 九月，己卯，魏以仲遠為太宰，庚辰，以爾朱天光為大司馬。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on jimao, Wei made Zhongyuan Grand Chancellor; on gengchen Erzhu Tianguang was made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Zhongyuan became Grand Chancellor; on gengchen Tianguang became Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，魏主追尊父廣陵惠王為先帝，母王氏為先太妃，封弟永業為高密王，子恕為勃海王。

translations.literal: On guisi the Wei emperor posthumously honored his father Prince of Guangling Hui as Former Emperor and his mother Lady Wang as Former Empress, enfeoffed his younger brother Yongye as Prince of Gaomi and his son Shu as Prince of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the emperor honored his father as Former Emperor and his mother as Former Empress, and enfeoffed Yongye and Shu as princes.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己酉，上幸同泰寺，升法座，講《涅槃經》，七日而罷。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on you, the emperor visited Tongtai Temple, ascended the dharma seat, and lectured on the Nirvana Sutra for seven days.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on you, the emperor lectured on the Nirvana Sutra at Tongtai Temple for seven days.

sentences.zh: 樂山侯正則，先有罪徙鬱林，招誘亡命，欲攻番禺，廣州刺史元景仲討斬之。
