translations.literal: Marquis of Leshan Zhengzhe, who had earlier been punished and banished to Yulin, gathered fugitives and wished to attack Panyu; Guangzhou inspector Yuan Jingzhong attacked and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Leshan Zhengzhe, banished to Yulin, gathered outlaws to attack Panyu; Jingzhong beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 正則，正德之弟也。

translations.literal: Zhengzhe was a younger brother of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengzhe was Zhengde's brother.

sentences.zh: 孫騰說高歡曰：「今朝廷隔絕，號令無所稟，不權有所立，則眾將沮散。

translations.literal: Sun Teng said to Gao Huan, "Now the court is cut off and orders have nowhere to come from; unless we set up someone provisionally, the generals will lose heart and scatter."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng told Huan, "The court is cut off—without a provisional ruler the army will scatter."

sentences.zh: 」歡疑之，騰再三固請，乃立勃海太守元朗為帝。

translations.literal: " Huan hesitated; Teng pressed again and again, and he then set Bohai prefect Yuan Lang as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Huan hesitated; Teng pressed until Huan set Bohai prefect Yuan Lang as emperor.

sentences.zh: 朗，融之子也。

translations.literal: Lang was a son of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Lang was Rong's son.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，朗即位於信都城西，改元中興。

translations.literal: On renyin Lang was enthroned west of Xindu city and changed the era name to Zhongxing.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Lang was enthroned west of Xindu and took the era name Zhongxing.

sentences.zh: 以歡為侍中、丞相、都督中外諸軍事、大將軍、錄尚書事、大行台，高乾為侍中、司空，高敖曹為驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、冀州刺史，孫騰為尚書左僕射，河北行台魏蘭根為右僕射。

translations.literal: Huan was made Palace Attendant, Chancellor, Supervisor of Military Affairs for All Armies, Grand General, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Commissioner; Gao Gan Palace Attendant and Minister of Works; Gao Aocao General of Agile Cavalry, Staff Equal to the Three Dukes, and Jizhou inspector; Sun Teng Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Hebei Route Commissioner Wei Langen Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Huan became chancellor and grand commander; Gan Minister of Works; Aocao General of Agile Cavalry and Jizhou inspector; Teng and Langen vice directors of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 己酉，爾朱仲遠、度律與驃騎大將軍斛斯椿、車騎大將軍、儀同三司賀拔勝、車騎大將軍賈顯智軍於陽平。

translations.literal: On you, Erzhu Zhongyuan, Dulu, General of Agile Cavalry Husi Chun, Chariot and Cavalry General and Staff Equal to the Three Dukes Heba Sheng, and Chariot and Cavalry General Jia Xianzhi encamped at Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: On you, Zhongyuan, Dulu, Husi Chun, Heba Sheng, and Jia Xianzhi camped at Yangping.

sentences.zh: 顯智名智，以字行，顯度之弟也。

translations.literal: Xianzhi's taboo name was Zhi; he went by his style. He was a younger brother of Xiandu.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi used his style Zhi; he was Xiandu's brother.

sentences.zh: 爾朱兆出井陘，軍於廣阿，眾號十萬。

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhao came out of Jingxing and encamped at Guang'a with a host said to number one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao came through Jingxing and camped at Guang'a with a host said to be one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 高歡縱反間，云「世隆兄弟謀殺兆」，復云「兆與歡同謀殺仲遠等」，由是迭相猜貳，徘徊不進。

translations.literal: Gao Huan spread counter-intelligence, saying "Shilong and his brothers plan to kill Zhao," and again that "Zhao and Huan together plan to kill Zhongyuan and the others." From this they suspected one another in turn and hesitated to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Huan spread rumors that Shilong would kill Zhao and that Zhao plotted with Huan against Zhongyuan, so they suspected one another and stalled.

sentences.zh: 仲遠等屢使斛斯椿、賀拔勝往諭兆，兆帥輕騎三百來就仲遠，同坐幕下，意色不平，手舞馬鞭，長嘯凝望，疑仲遠等有變，遂趨出，馳還。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan and the others repeatedly sent Husi Chun and Heba Sheng to instruct Zhao; Zhao led three hundred light horsemen to join Zhongyuan, sat together under the tent, looked ill at ease, waved his horsewhip, gazed long with a loud cry, suspected Zhongyuan and the others of treachery, then rushed out and galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Chun and Sheng to Zhao; he came with three hundred horse, sat uneasily with Zhongyuan, then fled back suspecting treachery.

sentences.zh: 仲遠遣椿、勝等追，曉說之，兆執棒、勝還營。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan sent Chun, Sheng, and others in pursuit, and at dawn persuaded him; Zhao seized Chun and Sheng and returned to camp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan sent Chun and Sheng after him; at dawn they brought him back with Chun and Sheng in custody.

sentences.zh: 仲遠、度律大懼，引兵南遁。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan and Dulu were greatly afraid and led their troops south in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan and Dulu fled south in terror.

sentences.zh: 兆數勝罪，將斬之，曰：「爾殺衛可孤，罪一也；

translations.literal: Zhao counted Sheng's crimes and was about to execute him, saying, "You killed Wei Ke'gu—crime one;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao listed Sheng's crimes: "You killed Wei Ke'gu—first crime;

sentences.zh: 天柱薨，爾不與世隆等俱來，而東征仲遠，罪二也。

translations.literal: when the Pillar died you did not come with Shilong and the others but marched east against Zhongyuan—crime two.
translations.idiomatic: when the Pillar fell you did not join Shilong but attacked Zhongyuan—second crime;

sentences.zh: 我欲殺爾久矣，今復何言？

translations.literal: I have long wished to kill you—what more is there to say?"
translations.idiomatic: I have long wanted you dead—what more is there?"

sentences.zh: 」勝曰：「可孤為國巨患，勝父子誅之，其功不小，反以為罪乎？

translations.literal: " Sheng said, "Ke'gu was a great peril to the state; my father and I killed him—a merit not small, yet you call it crime?
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said, "Ke'gu endangered the state; my father and I killed him—a great merit, yet you call it crime?"

sentences.zh: 天柱被戮，以君誅臣，勝寧負王，不負朝廷。

translations.literal: The Pillar was executed as subject by ruler; Sheng would rather wrong the king than wrong the court.
translations.idiomatic: The Pillar died as a subject; I would wrong the king rather than the court."

sentences.zh: 今日之事，生死在王。

translations.literal: Today's affair: life and death are in your hands.
translations.idiomatic: Today life and death are yours."

sentences.zh: 但寇賊密邇，骨肉構隙，自古及今，未有如是而不亡者。

translations.literal: But bandits press close and kin turn on kin—from antiquity to now none has been thus and not perished.
translations.idiomatic: Yet enemies are near and kin fight kin—none who do so survive."

sentences.zh: 勝不憚死，恐王失策。

translations.literal: Sheng does not fear death; I fear the king will err in strategy."
translations.idiomatic: I do not fear death; I fear you will err."

sentences.zh: 」兆乃捨之。

translations.literal: " Zhao then spared him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao spared him.

sentences.zh: 高歡將與兆戰，而畏其眾強，以問親信都督段韶，韶曰：「所謂眾者，得眾人之死；

translations.literal: Gao Huan was about to fight Zhao but feared his host was strong and asked his trusted commander Duan Shao. Shao said, "What is called 'many' is gaining the death of the multitude;
translations.idiomatic: Huan meant to fight Zhao but feared his numbers and asked Duan Shao, who said, "Numbers mean men willing to die for you;

sentences.zh: 所謂強者，得天下之心。

translations.literal: what is called 'strong' is gaining the heart of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: strength means winning the realm's heart."

sentences.zh: 爾朱氏上弒天子，中屠公卿，下暴百姓，王以順討逆，如湯沃雪，何眾強之有！

translations.literal: The Erzhu murdered the Son of Heaven above, slaughtered the nobles in the middle, and oppressed the people below; the king punishes rebellion with justice like boiling water on snow—what multitude or strength is there!"
translations.idiomatic: The Erzhu killed the emperor, butchered the court, and ravaged the people—you strike them with justice as snow melts in boiling water—what numbers or strength remain?"

sentences.zh: 」歡曰：「雖然，吾以小敵大，恐無天命不能濟也。

translations.literal: " Huan said, "Even so, I use the small against the large and fear that without Heaven's mandate it cannot succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Huan said, "Still, small against large—I fear Heaven's mandate may fail me."

sentences.zh: 」韶曰：「韶聞『小能敵大，小道大淫。

translations.literal: " Shao said, "Shao has heard, 'The small can overcome the large; the small Way overcomes great excess.
translations.idiomatic: Shao said, "The small can overcome the large; excess destroys itself."

sentences.zh: 』『皇天無親，唯德是輔。

translations.literal: ' 'Heaven has no favorites—it aids virtue alone.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has no favorites—it aids virtue alone."

sentences.zh: 』爾朱氏外亂天下，內失英雄心，智者不為謀，勇者不為鬥，人心已去，天意安有不從者哉！

translations.literal: ' The Erzhu disorder the realm without and lose heroes' hearts within; the wise will not plot for them, the brave will not fight for them—hearts are gone; how could Heaven's intent not follow!"
translations.idiomatic: The Erzhu ravage the realm and lose every hero—who would plot or fight for them? Hearts are gone; Heaven must be with you!"

sentences.zh: 」韶，榮之子也。

translations.literal: " Shao was Rong's son.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was Rong's son.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，歡大破兆於廣阿，俘其甲卒五千餘人。

translations.literal: On xinhai Huan routed Zhao at Guang'a and captured more than five thousand armored soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Huan crushed Zhao at Guang'a and took more than five thousand armored men.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙未，上幸同泰寺，講《般若經》，七日而罷。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on yiwei, the emperor visited Tongtai Temple and lectured on the Prajna Sutra for seven days.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yiwei, the emperor lectured on the Prajna Sutra at Tongtai for seven days.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，魏高歡引兵攻鄴，相州刺史劉誕嬰城固守。

translations.literal: On gengchen Wei's Gao Huan led troops against Ye; Xiangzhou inspector Liu Dan closed the city and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Huan besieged Ye; Liu Dan held the walls.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏南兗州城民王乞得劫刺史劉世明，舉州來降。

translations.literal: That year the people of Southern Yanzhou city seized inspector Liu Shiming and offered the province in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: That year Southern Yanzhou townspeople seized Liu Shiming and surrendered the province.

sentences.zh: 世明，芳之族子也。

translations.literal: Shiming was a clansman of Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Shiming was Fang's kinsman.

sentences.zh: 上以侍中元樹為鎮北將軍、都督北討諸軍事，鎮譙城。

translations.literal: The emperor made Palace Attendant Yuan Shu Grand General Who Guards the North and commander of northern campaigns, garrisoned at Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Yuan Shu Grand General Who Guards the North and stationed him at Qiao.

sentences.zh: 以世明為征西大將軍、郢州刺史，加儀同三司。

translations.literal: Shiming was made Grand General Who Campaigns West and Yingzhou inspector, with the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Shiming was made Grand General Who Campaigns West and Yingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 世明不受，固請北歸，上許之。

translations.literal: Shiming would not accept and firmly asked to return north; the emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Shiming refused and begged to go north; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 世明至洛陽，奉送所持節，歸鄉里，不仕而卒。

translations.literal: Shiming reached Luoyang, returned his credentials, went home, did not serve, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Luoyang, returned his staff, went home, and died without office.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝十一中大通四年（

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang, year eleven of Zhongdatong (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang, year eleven of Zhongdatong (

sentences.zh: 壬子，公元五三二年）

translations.literal: renzi, 532 CE)
translations.idiomatic: renzi, 532 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙寅，以南平王偉為大司馬，元法僧為太尉，袁昂為司空。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on bingyin, Prince of Nanping Wei was made Grand Marshal, Yuan Faseng Grand Marshal, and Yuan Ang Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on bingyin, Prince of Nanping Wei became Grand Marshal, Faseng Grand Marshal, and Ang Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 立西豐侯正德為臨賀王。

translations.literal: Marquis of Xifeng Zhengde was made Prince of Linhe.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Xifeng Zhengde was made Prince of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 正德自結於朱異，上既封昭明諸子，異言正德失職，故王之。

translations.literal: Zhengde had attached himself to Zhu Yi; after the emperor enfeoffed Zhaoming's sons, Yi said Zhengde had lost his place, and therefore he was made prince.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde had courted Zhu Yi; after Zhaoming's sons were enfeoffed, Yi said Zhengde was passed over, so he received a princedom.

sentences.zh: 以太子右衛率薛法護為司州牧，衛送魏王悅入洛。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Right Guard Commander Xue Fahu was made Sizhou governor and escorted Prince of Runan Yue into Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Fahu was made Sizhou governor to escort Prince of Runan Yue to Luo.

sentences.zh: 庚午，立太子綱之長子大器為宣城王。

translations.literal: On gengwu the crown prince's eldest son Daqi was made Prince of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Daqi, the crown prince's eldest son, was made Prince of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 魏高歡攻鄴，為地道，施柱而焚之，城陷入地。

translations.literal: Wei's Gao Huan attacked Ye, dug tunnels, set pillars and burned them, and the wall sank into the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Huan attacked Ye, undermined the walls with fire, and a section collapsed.

sentences.zh: 壬午，拔鄴，擒劉誕，以楊愔為行台右丞。

translations.literal: On renwu Ye was taken, Liu Dan captured, and Yang Yin made Eastern Route Right Assistant of the Grand Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Ye fell, Dan was captured, and Yang Yin became Eastern Route Right Assistant.

sentences.zh: 時軍國多事，文檄教令，皆出於愔及開府咨議參軍崔凌。

translations.literal: At the time military and state affairs were many; proclamations and orders all came from Yin and Staff Consultant Cui Ling of the Chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: Proclamations and orders came from Yin and Staff Consultant Cui Ling.

sentences.zh: 凌，逞之五世孫也。

translations.literal: Ling was a fifth-generation descendant of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ling was a fifth-generation descendant of Cheng.

sentences.zh: 二月，以太尉元法僧為東魏王，欲遣還北，兗州刺史羊侃為軍司馬，與法僧偕行。

translations.literal: Second month: Grand Marshal Yuan Faseng was made Prince of Eastern Wei and was to be sent back north; Yanzhou inspector Yang Kan was army marshal and went with Faseng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Faseng was made Prince of Eastern Wei to return north; Yang Kan went as army marshal.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史邵陵王綸遣人就市，賒買錦彩絲布數百匹，市人皆閉邸店不出；

translations.literal: Prince of Shaoling Lun sent men to the market to buy several hundred bolts of brocade and silk on credit; the merchants all closed their shops and would not sell.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shaoling Lun sent men to buy hundreds of bolts of silk on credit; merchants shut their shops.

sentences.zh: 少府丞何智通依事啟聞。

translations.literal: Assistant in the Palace Storehouse He Zhitong reported according to regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Storehouse assistant He Zhitong reported it.

sentences.zh: 綸被責還第，乃遣防閣戴子高等以槊刺智通於都巷，刃出於背。

translations.literal: Lun was rebuked and sent back to his residence; he then sent guard Dai Zigao and others to stab Zhitong in a capital lane with spears, the blades coming out his back.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was rebuked and confined; he sent Dai Zigao to stab Zhitong in the street, spear through his back.

sentences.zh: 智通識子高，取其血以指畫車壁為「邵陵」字，乃絕，由是事覺。

translations.literal: Zhitong recognized Zigao, took his blood and with a finger wrote "Shaoling" on a carriage wall, then died; from this the affair was discovered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhitong knew Zigao, wrote "Shaoling" in blood on a cart, and died—the crime was exposed.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，綸坐免為庶人，鎖之於第，經三旬，乃脫鎖，頃之，復封爵。

translations.literal: On gengxu Lun was demoted to commoner for his crime, chained in his residence; after thirty days the chains were removed, and soon his title was restored.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Lun was reduced to commoner, chained at home; after thirty days he was unchained and soon restored.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，魏安定王追謚敬宗曰武懷皇帝，甲子，以高歡為丞相、柱國大將軍、太師；

translations.literal: On xinhai Wei's Prince of Anding posthumously honored Emperor Jingzong as Emperor Wu Huai; on jiazi Gao Huan was made Chancellor, Pillar of State Grand General, and Grand Preceptor;
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Anding posthumously honored Jingzong as Wu Huai; on jiazi Huan became chancellor, pillar grand general, and grand preceptor;

sentences.zh: 三月，丙寅，以高澄為驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: Third month, on bingyin Gao Cheng was made General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingyin Gao Cheng became General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，安定王帥百官入居於鄴。

translations.literal: On dingchou the Prince of Anding led the hundred officials to take up residence at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Anding and the officials moved into Ye.

sentences.zh: 爾朱兆與爾朱世隆等互相猜阻，世隆卑辭厚禮諭兆，欲使之赴洛，唯其所欲，又請節閔帝納兆女為後；

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhao and Erzhu Shilong and the others suspected one another; Shilong used humble words and rich gifts to persuade Zhao, wishing him to come to Luo and have whatever he wished, and also asked that Emperor Jiemin take Zhao's daughter as empress;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao and Shilong mistrusted one another; Shilong flattered Zhao with gifts and urged him to Luo, offering him whatever he wished, and asked Jiemin to marry Zhao's daughter;

sentences.zh: 兆乃悅，並與天光、度律更立誓約，復相親睦。

translations.literal: Zhao was pleased, and with Tianguang and Dulu renewed their oaths and were friendly again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was pleased; he, Tianguang, and Dulu renewed their oaths and made peace.

sentences.zh: 斛斯椿陰謂賀拔勝曰：「天下皆怨毒爾朱，而吾等為之用，亡無日矣，不如圖之。

translations.literal: Husi Chun secretly said to Heba Sheng, "All under Heaven hate the Erzhu, yet we serve them—we will perish any day; better plot against them."
translations.idiomatic: Husi Chun whispered to Heba Sheng, "The realm hates the Erzhu yet we serve them—we die any day; we should strike first."

sentences.zh: 」勝曰：「天光與兆各據一方，欲盡去之甚難，去之不盡，必為後患，奈何？

translations.literal: " Sheng said, "Tianguang and Zhao each hold a region; to remove them all is very hard, and those not removed will surely be a later trouble—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said, "Tianguang and Zhao hold separate regions—to remove them all is hard, and survivors will haunt us—what then?"

sentences.zh: 」椿曰：「此易致耳。

translations.literal: " Chun said, "That is easy to bring about."
translations.idiomatic: Chun said, "That is easy."

sentences.zh: 」乃說世隆追天光等赴洛，共討高歡。

translations.literal: " He then persuaded Shilong to summon Tianguang and the others to Luo to attack Gao Huan together.
translations.idiomatic: He persuaded Shilong to summon Tianguang to Luo to join against Huan.

sentences.zh: 世隆屢征天光，天光不至，使椿自往邀之，曰：「高歡作亂，非王不能定，豈可坐視宗族夷滅邪！

translations.literal: Shilong repeatedly summoned Tianguang; Tianguang did not come. Shilong sent Chun in person to invite him, saying, "Gao Huan is in rebellion—only you, my prince, can settle it; can you sit and watch the clan destroyed!"
translations.idiomatic: Shilong summoned Tianguang in vain and sent Chun, saying, "Huan rebels—only you can save the clan!"

sentences.zh: 」天光不得已，將東出，問策於雍州刺史賀拔岳，岳曰：「王家跨據三方，士馬殷盛，高歡烏合之眾，豈能為敵！

translations.literal: " Tianguang had no choice and was about to march east; he asked Yongzhou inspector Heba Yue for counsel. Yue said, "Your house holds three regions, troops and horses abundant—Gao Huan's rabble cannot be your match!
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang must march east and asked Heba Yue, who said, "Your house holds three regions—Huan's rabble cannot match you!

sentences.zh: 但能同心戮力，往無不捷。

translations.literal: Only unite in heart and strength and you will succeed wherever you go.
translations.idiomatic: Unite and you cannot fail."

sentences.zh: 若骨肉相疑，則圖存之不暇，安能制人！

translations.literal: If kin suspect kin, you will scarce save yourselves—how can you control others!
translations.idiomatic: If kin turn on kin, you will not save yourselves—how rule others?"

sentences.zh: 如下官所見，莫若且鎮關中以固根本，分遣銳師與眾軍合勢，進可以克敵，退可以自全。

translations.literal: As I see it, better hold Guanzhong to secure the root, send picked troops to join the host, advance to conquer, retreat to preserve yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Hold Guanzhong, send picked troops to join the main army—advance to win, retreat to survive."

sentences.zh: 」天光不從。

translations.literal: " Tianguang did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang would not listen.

sentences.zh: 閏月，壬寅，天光自長安，兆自晉陽，度律自洛陽，仲遠自東郡，皆會於鄴，眾號二十萬，夾洹水而軍，節閔帝以長孫稚為大行台，總督之。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, on renyin: Tianguang from Chang'an, Zhao from Jinyang, Dulu from Luoyang, Zhongyuan from Dong commandery—all met at Ye, a host said to be two hundred thousand, camped on both banks of the Huan River. Emperor Jiemin made Changsun Zhi Grand Commissioner to command them.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Tianguang, Zhao, Dulu, and Zhongyuan converged at Ye with two hundred thousand men along the Huan; Jiemin put Changsun Zhi in command.

sentences.zh: 高歡令吏部尚書封隆之守鄴，癸丑，出頓紫陌，大都督高敖曹將鄉里部曲王桃湯等三千人以從。

translations.literal: Gao Huan ordered Minister of the Civil Service Feng Longzhi to hold Ye; on guichou he encamped at Zimo. Grand Commander Gao Aocao led three thousand local followers such as Wang Taotang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan left Feng Longzhi at Ye and on guichou camped at Zimo; Aocao led three thousand local troops.

sentences.zh: 歡曰：「高都督所將皆漢兵，恐不足集事，欲割鮮卑兵千餘人相雜用之，何如？

translations.literal: Huan said, "Commander Gao's men are all Han soldiers—I fear they are not enough for the task. I wish to cut off more than a thousand Xianbei soldiers to mix with them—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Huan said, "Your men are all Han—I fear that is not enough; shall we mix in a thousand Xianbei?"

sentences.zh: 」敖曹曰：「敖曹所將，練習已久，前後格鬥，不減鮮卑。

translations.literal: " Aocao said, "Those I lead have long been drilled; in repeated fights they are no less than Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: Aocao said, "My men are drilled; in fight they match Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 今若雜之，情不相洽，勝則爭功，退則推罪，不煩更配也。

translations.literal: If we mix them now, hearts will not agree—if victorious they will fight for credit, if defeated they will push blame on others. No need to reassign."
translations.idiomatic: Mix them and hearts divide—victory brings quarrels, defeat brings blame. No need to reassign."

sentences.zh: 庚申，爾朱兆帥輕騎三千夜襲鄴城，叩西門，不克而退。

translations.literal: On gengshen Erzhu Zhao led three thousand light horsemen in a night raid on Ye city, knocked at the west gate, could not take it, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Zhao raided Ye by night with three thousand horse, failed at the west gate, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，歡將戰馬不滿二千，步兵不滿三萬，眾寡不敵，乃於韓陵為圓陣，連繫牛驢以塞歸道，於是將士皆有死志。

translations.literal: On renxu Huan had fewer than two thousand war horses and fewer than thirty thousand foot soldiers; the odds were against him. He formed a circular array at Hanling, tethered oxen and donkeys to block the retreat route, and thus officers and men all had the will to die.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Huan had under two thousand horse and thirty thousand foot; at Hanling he formed a ring, tethered cattle to block retreat, and gave his men the will to die.

sentences.zh: 兆望見歡，遙責歡以叛己，歡曰：「本所以戮力者，共輔帝室。

translations.literal: Zhao saw Huan from afar and rebuked him for betraying him. Huan said, "We joined forces at first to support the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao rebuked Huan for betrayal; Huan said, "We joined to serve the throne.

sentences.zh: 今天子何在？

translations.literal: Where is the Son of Heaven today?"
translations.idiomatic: Where is the emperor today?"

sentences.zh: 」兆曰：「永安枉害天柱，我報仇耳。

translations.literal: " Zhao said, "Yongan wrongly killed the Pillar—I am avenging him."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, "Yongan murdered the Pillar—I avenge him."

sentences.zh: 」歡曰：「我昔親聞天柱計，汝在戶前立，豈得言不反邪！

translations.literal: Huan said, "I heard the Pillar's plan with my own ears—you stood before the door; can you say you did not rebel!
translations.idiomatic: Huan said, "I heard the Pillar's plan—you stood at the door; do not say you did not rebel!

sentences.zh: 且以君殺臣，何報之有！

translations.literal: Moreover, when a subject kills his lord, what vengeance is there!
translations.idiomatic: A subject kills his lord—what vengeance is that?"

sentences.zh: 今日義絕矣！

translations.literal: Today righteousness is ended!"
translations.idiomatic: Today we are enemies!"

sentences.zh: 」遂戰。

translations.literal: They fought.
translations.idiomatic: They fought.

sentences.zh: 歡將中軍，高敖曹將左軍，歡從父弟岳將右軍。

translations.literal: Huan commanded the center army; Gao Aocao the left; Huan's cousin Yue the right.
translations.idiomatic: Huan held the center, Aocao the left, cousin Yue the right.

sentences.zh: 歡戰不利，兆等乘之，岳以五百騎沖其前，別將斛律敦收散卒躡其後，敖曹以千騎自栗園出橫擊之，兆等大敗，賀拔勝與徐州刺史杜德於陣降歡。

translations.literal: Huan's battle went badly and Zhao and the others pressed him. Yue charged their front with five hundred horse; another commander Hulu Dun gathered scattered troops and followed their rear; Aocao with a thousand horse struck from Chestnut Garden on the flank. Zhao and the others were routed; Heba Sheng and Xuzhou inspector Du De surrendered to Huan in the field.
translations.idiomatic: Huan faltered; Yue charged with five hundred horse, Dun harried the rear, Aocao struck from the flank; Zhao was routed; Sheng and Du De surrendered.

sentences.zh: 兆對慕容紹宗撫膺曰：「不用公言，以至於此！

translations.literal: Zhao clutched his breast to Murong Shaozong and said, "Had I taken your counsel, it would not have come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao told Shaozong, "Had I listened to you, this would not have happened!"

sentences.zh: 」欲輕騎西走，紹宗反旗鳴角，收散卒成軍而去。

translations.literal: He wished to flee west with light horse; Shaozong turned the banners, sounded the horns, gathered scattered troops, and withdrew in formation.
translations.idiomatic: He fled west; Shaozong rallied the broken troops and withdrew in order.

sentences.zh: 兆還晉陽，仲遠奔東郡。

translations.literal: Zhao returned to Jinyang; Zhongyuan fled to Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao fled to Jinyang; Zhongyuan to Dong commandery.

sentences.zh: 爾朱彥伯聞度律等敗，欲自將兵守河橋，世隆不從。

translations.literal: Erzhu Yanbo heard Dulu and the others were defeated and wished to lead troops himself to hold Heqiao; Shilong would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo heard of the defeat and wished to hold Heqiao; Shilong refused.

sentences.zh: 度律、天光將之洛陽，大都督斛斯椿謂都督賈顯度、賈顯智曰：「今不先執爾朱氏，吾屬死無類矣。

translations.literal: Dulu and Tianguang were about to go to Luoyang. Grand Commander Husi Chun said to commanders Jia Xiandu and Jia Xianzhi, "If we do not seize the Erzhu first, we are dead men."
translations.idiomatic: Dulu and Tianguang marched on Luo; Chun told the Jia brothers, "Seize the Erzhu first or we perish."

sentences.zh: 」乃夜於桑下盟，約倍道先還。

translations.literal: " That night they allied under a mulberry tree and agreed to double-march back first.
translations.idiomatic: That night they swore under a mulberry to race back first.

sentences.zh: 世隆使其外兵參軍陽叔淵單騎馳赴北中，簡閱敗眾，以次內之。

translations.literal: Shilong sent his outer-army adjutant Yang Shuyuan alone on horseback to rush to North Central, review the defeated troops, and admit them in order.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong sent Yang Shuyuan to North Central to admit the defeated in order.

sentences.zh: 椿至，不得入城，乃詭說叔淵曰：「天光部下皆是西人，聞欲大掠洛邑，遷都長安，宜先內我以為之備。

translations.literal: When Chun arrived he could not enter the city and deceived Shuyuan, saying, "Tianguang's men are all westerners; hearing they mean to plunder Luoyang and move the capital to Chang'an, you should admit me first to prepare."
translations.idiomatic: Chun could not enter and lied to Shuyuan that Tianguang's westerners meant to sack Luo and move the capital—admit me first to guard against it.

sentences.zh: 」叔淵信之。

translations.literal: Shuyuan believed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyuan believed him.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲子朔，椿等入據河橋，盡殺爾朱氏之黨。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, first day jiazi: Chun and the others seized Heqiao and killed all the Erzhu party.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi in the fourth month Chun seized Heqiao and slaughtered the Erzhu party.

sentences.zh: 度律、天光欲攻之，會大雨晝夜不止，士馬疲頓，弓矢不可施，遂西走，至灅陂津，為人所擒，送於椿所。

translations.literal: Dulu and Tianguang wished to attack them, but great rain fell day and night without cease; men and horses were exhausted and bows could not be drawn; they fled west and at Lebei ford were seized and sent to Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Dulu and Tianguang attacked, but rain exhausted men and horses; they fled west and were captured at Lebei and sent to Chun.

sentences.zh: 椿使行台長孫稚詣洛陽奏狀，別使賈顯智、張歡帥騎掩襲世隆，執之。

translations.literal: Chun sent Eastern Route Commissioner Changsun Zhi to Luoyang to report and separately sent Jia Xianzhi and Zhang Huan with horse to seize Shilong; he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Chun sent Changsun Zhi to report and Jia Xianzhi and Zhang Huan to seize Shilong.

sentences.zh: 彥伯時在禁直，長孫稚於神虎門啟陳：「高歡義功既振，請誅爾朱氏。

translations.literal: Yanbo was then on palace duty; Changsun Zhi reported at the Divine Tiger Gate: "Gao Huan's righteous merit has risen—please execute the Erzhu."
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo was on duty; Changsun Zhi asked Jiemin to execute the Erzhu now that Huan had triumphed.

sentences.zh: 」節閔帝使舍人郭崇報彥伯，彥伯狼狽走出，為人所執，與世隆俱斬於閶闔門外，送其首並度律、天光於高歡。

translations.literal: Emperor Jiemin sent Attendant Guo Chong to inform Yanbo; Yanbo fled in panic and was seized; he and Shilong were beheaded together outside the Changhe Gate, and their heads with those of Dulu and Tianguang were sent to Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiemin sent Guo Chong to Yanbo; Yanbo fled and was seized; he and Shilong were beheaded at Changhe Gate; their heads and Dulu's and Tianguang's were sent to Huan.

sentences.zh: 節閔帝使中書舍人盧辯勞歡於鄴，歡使之見安定王，辯抗辭不從，歡不能奪，乃捨之。

translations.literal: Emperor Jiemin sent Palace Scribe Lu Bian to comfort Huan at Ye. Huan had him see the Prince of Anding; Bian refused with strong words and Huan could not force him, so he let him go.
translations.idiomatic: Jiemin sent Lu Bian to Ye; Huan had him see Anding; Bian refused; Huan let him go.

sentences.zh: 辯，同之兄子也。

translations.literal: Bian was a nephew of Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was Tong's nephew.

sentences.zh: 辛未，驃騎大將軍、行濟州事侯景降於安定王。

translations.literal: On xinwei General of Agile Cavalry and acting Jizhou commander Hou Jing surrendered to the Prince of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Hou Jing surrendered to Anding.

sentences.zh: 以景為尚書僕射、南道大行台、濟州刺史。

translations.literal: Jing was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Southern Route Grand Commissioner, and Jizhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Jing became vice director, southern route commissioner, and Jizhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 爾朱仲遠來奔。

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhongyuan came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan came over in surrender.

sentences.zh: 仲遠帳下都督喬寧、張子期自滑台詣歡降。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan's commanders Qiao Ning and Zhang Ziqi of Huatai came to Huan in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders Qiao Ning and Zhang Ziqi came from Huatai to surrender.

sentences.zh: 歡責之曰：「汝事仲遠，擅其榮利，盟契百重，許同生死。

translations.literal: Huan rebuked them: "You served Zhongyuan and monopolized his honors; oaths were piled a hundredfold and you swore to live and die together.
translations.idiomatic: Huan rebuked them: "You shared Zhongyuan's honors and swore to live and die with him.

sentences.zh: 前仲遠自徐州為逆，妝為戎首；

translations.literal: Earlier when Zhongyuan rebelled from Xuzhou you played the barbarian chief;
translations.idiomatic: When he rebelled from Xuzhou you played his chief;

sentences.zh: 今仲遠南走，汝復叛之。

translations.literal: now that Zhongyuan flees south you betray him again.
translations.idiomatic: now he flees south and you betray him again.

sentences.zh: 事天子則不忠，事仲遠則無信，犬馬尚識飼之者，汝曾犬馬之不如！

translations.literal: Loyal to the Son of Heaven you are not; faithful to Zhongyuan you are not—even dogs know who feeds them; you are worse than dogs!"
translations.idiomatic: You are not loyal to the emperor nor faithful to Zhongyuan—even dogs know their master; you are beneath dogs!"

sentences.zh: 」遂斬之。

translations.literal: He then beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded them.

sentences.zh: 爾朱天光之東下也，留其弟顯壽鎮長安，召秦州刺史侯莫陳悅，欲與之俱東。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Tianguang marched east he left his younger brother Xianshou to hold Chang'an and summoned Qinzhou inspector Houmochen Yue, wishing him to go east together.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianguang marched east he left Xianshou at Chang'an and summoned Houmochen Yue east.

sentences.zh: 賀拔岳知天光必敗，欲留悅共圖顯壽以應高歡，計未有所出。

translations.literal: Heba Yue knew Tianguang would surely be defeated and wished to keep Yue to join him in taking Xianshou to support Gao Huan, but had no plan.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Yue knew Tianguang would fall and wished to keep Yue to seize Xianshou for Huan, but had no plan.

sentences.zh: 宇文泰謂岳曰：「今天光尚近，悅未必有貳心，若以此告之，恐其驚懼。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai said to Yue, "Tianguang is still near; Yue may not yet be disloyal. If you tell him this outright, he may be alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai said, "Tianguang is near—Yue may not yet waver; tell him outright and he may panic.

sentences.zh: 然悅雖為主將，不能制物，若先說其眾，必人有留心。

translations.literal: Yet though Yue is commander-in-chief, he cannot control his men; if you first persuade his troops, some will surely hesitate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yue cannot control his men—persuade the troops first and some will hesitate.

sentences.zh: 悅進失爾朱之期，退恐人情變動，乘此說悅，事無不遂。

translations.literal: If Yue advances he misses the Erzhu deadline; if he retreats he fears the mood will change—use this moment to persuade Yue and nothing will fail."
translations.idiomatic: Advance and he misses the Erzhu; retreat and minds change—persuade him now and you cannot fail."

sentences.zh: 」岳大喜，即令泰入悅軍說之，悅遂與岳共襲長安。

translations.literal: Yue was greatly pleased and at once sent Tai into Yue's army to persuade him; Yue then joined Yue in attacking Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was delighted and sent Tai to Yue's army; Yue joined him against Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 泰帥輕騎為前驅，顯壽棄城走，追至華陰，擒之。

translations.literal: Tai led light horse as vanguard; Xianshou abandoned the city and fled; pursued to Huayin and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Tai led the van; Xianshou fled; they caught him at Huayin.

sentences.zh: 歡以岳為關西大行台，岳以泰為行台左丞，領府司馬，事無鉅細皆委之。

translations.literal: Huan made Yue Western Route Grand Commissioner; Yue made Tai Eastern Route Left Assistant and chief of the bureau—nothing great or small was entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan made Yue western commissioner; Yue entrusted everything to Tai.

sentences.zh: 爾朱世隆之拒高歡也，使齊州行台尚書房謨募兵趣四瀆，又使其弟青州刺史弼趣亂城，揚聲北渡，為掎角之勢。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Shilong resisted Gao Huan he sent Qizhou Route Commissioner Fang Mo to levy troops toward the Four Ferries and his younger brother Qingzhou inspector Bi toward Luancheng, proclaiming a crossing north as pincers.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong sent Fang Mo to levy troops at the Four Ferries and Bi toward Luancheng as a northern pincer.

sentences.zh: 及韓陵既敗，弼還東陽，聞世隆等死，欲來奔，數與左右割臂為盟。

translations.literal: After Hanling was lost Bi returned to Dongyang; hearing Shilong and the others were dead he wished to come over and several times cut his arm with his attendants in oath.
translations.idiomatic: After Hanling Bi returned to Dongyang; hearing Shilong was dead he wished to surrender and cut his arm in oath with his men.

sentences.zh: 帳下都督馮紹隆，素為弼所信待，說弼曰：「今方同契闊，宜更割心前之血以盟眾。

translations.literal: Commander Feng Shaolong, long trusted by Bi, said to Bi, "Now we share life and death—you should cut blood from before the heart to swear the host."
translations.idiomatic: Commander Feng Shaolong, whom Bi trusted, said, "Cut heart-blood to swear the host."

sentences.zh: 」弼從之，大集部下，披胸令紹隆割之。

translations.literal: Bi agreed, gathered his subordinates, bared his chest, and had Shaolong cut him.
translations.idiomatic: Bi agreed, bared his chest, and let Shaolong cut.

sentences.zh: 紹隆因推刃殺之，傳首洛陽。

translations.literal: Shaolong then drove the blade in and killed him and sent his head to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shaolong killed him and sent his head to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 丙子，安東將軍辛永以建州降於安定王。

translations.literal: On bingzi General Who Pacifies the East Xin Yong surrendered Jianzhou to the Prince of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Xin Yong surrendered Jianzhou to Anding.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，安定王至邙山。

translations.literal: On xinsi the Prince of Anding reached Mount Mang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Anding reached Mount Mang.

sentences.zh: 高歡以安定王疏遠，使僕射魏蘭根慰諭洛邑，且觀節閔帝之為人，欲復奉之。

translations.literal: Gao Huan, because the Prince of Anding was remote in kinship, sent Vice Director Wei Langen to comfort Luoyang and observe Emperor Jiemin's character, wishing to support him again.
translations.idiomatic: Huan thought Anding too remote in kin and sent Wei Langen to Luoyang to sound Jiemin, intending to restore him.

sentences.zh: 蘭根以帝神采高明，恐於後難制，與高乾兄弟及黃門侍郎崔凌共勸歡廢之。

translations.literal: Langen found the emperor's bearing lofty and feared he would be hard to control later; with the Gao brothers and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Cui Ling he urged Huan to depose him.
translations.idiomatic: Langen found Jiemin too sharp to control and with the Gao brothers and Cui Ling urged deposition.

sentences.zh: 歡集百官問所宜立，莫有應者，太僕代人綦毋俊盛稱節閔帝賢明，宜主社稷，歡欣然是之。

translations.literal: Huan assembled the hundred officials and asked whom to establish; none answered. Grand Servant Qiwu Jun of Dai greatly praised Jiemin as wise and fit to rule the altars; Huan was pleased and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Huan asked whom to enthrone; none spoke until Qiwu Jun praised Jiemin; Huan agreed.

sentences.zh: 凌作色曰：「若言賢明，自可待我高王，徐登大位。

translations.literal: Ling changed color and said, "If you call him wise, let him wait for our King Gao to ascend in time.
translations.idiomatic: Ling snapped, "If he is wise, let him wait for King Gao.

sentences.zh: 廣陵既為逆胡所立，何得猶為天子！

translations.literal: Guangling was set up by rebel barbarians—how can he still be Son of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Guangling was set up by barbarian rebels—how can he remain emperor!

sentences.zh: 若從俊言，王師何名義舉？

translations.literal: If we follow Jun's words, what righteous name has the king's army!"
translations.idiomatic: Follow Jun and our army has no righteous name!"

sentences.zh: 」歡遂幽節閔帝於崇訓佛寺。

translations.literal: Huan then imprisoned Emperor Jiemin at Chongxun Buddhist Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Huan imprisoned Jiemin at Chongxun Temple.

sentences.zh: 歡入洛陽，斛斯椿謂賀拔勝曰：「今天下事，在吾與君耳，若不先制人，將為人所制。

translations.literal: Huan entered Luoyang. Husi Chun said to Heba Sheng, "Today the realm's affair is in you and me; if we do not strike first we will be struck."
translations.idiomatic: In Luoyang Chun told Sheng, "The realm is ours to seize—strike first or be struck."

sentences.zh: 高歡初至，圖之不難。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan first arrived it would not have been hard to plot against him."
translations.idiomatic: When Huan first came it would have been easy."

sentences.zh: 」勝曰：「彼有功於時，害之不祥。

translations.literal: " Sheng said, "He has merit in the time—harming him is ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said, "He has merit—harm him and ill fortune follows.

sentences.zh: 比數夜與歡同宿，具序往昔之懷，兼荷兄恩意甚多，何苦憚之！

translations.literal: These several nights I have lodged with Huan; he told at length our old friendship and how much he owes my elder brother's kindness—why fear him!"
translations.idiomatic: I have lodged with him; he spoke of old friendship and my brother's kindness—why fear him!"

sentences.zh: 」椿乃止。

translations.literal: Chun then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Chun desisted.

sentences.zh: 歡以汝南王悅，高祖之子，召欲立之，聞其狂暴無常，乃止。

translations.literal: Huan wished to set up Prince of Runan Yue, a son of Emperor Gaozu, but hearing he was violent and inconstant he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Huan wished to set up Prince of Runan Yue, Gaozu's son, but heard he was violent and desisted.

sentences.zh: 時諸王多逃匿，尚書左僕射平陽王修，懷之子也，匿於田舍。

translations.literal: At the time many princes had fled and hidden; Left Vice Director Prince of Pingyang Xiu, a son of Huai, hid in a farmstead.
translations.idiomatic: Many princes hid; Prince of Pingyang Xiu, Huai's son, hid in the fields.

sentences.zh: 歡欲立之，使斛斯椿求之。

translations.literal: Huan wished to set him up and sent Husi Chun to find him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan wished to enthrone Xiu and sent Chun to find him.

sentences.zh: 椿見修所親員外散騎侍郎太原王思政，問王所在，思政曰：「須知問意。

translations.literal: Chun saw Xiu's associate Gentleman of Scattered Cavalry Wang Sizheng of Taiyuan and asked where the prince was. Sizheng said, "I must know your intent."
translations.idiomatic: Chun asked Wang Sizheng where Xiu was; Sizheng said, "Tell me your intent."

sentences.zh: 」椿曰：「欲立為天子。

translations.literal: Chun said, "I wish to set him up as Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Chun said, "To make him emperor."

sentences.zh: 」思政乃言之。

translations.literal: Sizheng then told him.
translations.idiomatic: Sizheng told him.

sentences.zh: 椿從思政見修，修色變，謂思政曰：「得無賣我邪？

translations.literal: Chun followed Sizheng to see Xiu. Xiu changed color and said to Sizheng, "You are not selling me out?"
translations.idiomatic: Chun saw Xiu, who asked Sizheng, "You are not selling me?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「不也。

translations.literal: He said, "No."
translations.idiomatic: "No."

sentences.zh: 」曰：「敢保之乎？

translations.literal: "Can you guarantee it?"
translations.idiomatic: "Can you guarantee it?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「變態百端，何可保也？

translations.literal: "Moods change a hundred ways—how can one guarantee!"
translations.idiomatic: "Moods shift—who can guarantee?"

sentences.zh: 」椿馳報歡。

translations.literal: Chun galloped to report to Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Chun rode to tell Huan.

sentences.zh: 歡遣四百騎迎修入氈帳，陳誠，泣下沾襟，修讓以寡德，歡再拜，修亦拜。

translations.literal: Huan sent four hundred horse to welcome Xiu into the felt tent, spoke sincerely, and tears wet his lapels. Xiu declined for lack of virtue; Huan bowed twice and Xiu bowed in return.
translations.idiomatic: Huan sent four hundred horse, welcomed Xiu to his tent with tears; Xiu demurred; both bowed.

sentences.zh: 歡出備服御，進湯沐，達夜嚴警。

translations.literal: Huan brought out prepared robes and viands, offered bath and rest, and kept strict guard all night.
translations.idiomatic: Huan gave robes, food, and bath, and guarded him all night.

sentences.zh: 昧爽，文武執鞭以朝，使斛斯椿奉勸進表。

translations.literal: At dawn civil and military officials came holding whips in court; he had Husi Chun present the memorial urging enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn officials came with whips; Chun presented the enthronement memorial.

sentences.zh: 椿入帷門，磬折延首而不敢前，修令思政取表視之，曰：「便不得不稱朕矣。

translations.literal: Chun entered the curtain gate, bowed low with head extended and dared not advance. Xiu had Sizheng take the memorial and read it, saying, "I can no longer avoid calling myself 'I.'"
translations.idiomatic: Chun bowed at the curtain; Xiu had Sizheng read the memorial: "I can no longer refuse the throne."

sentences.zh: 」乃為安定王作詔策而禪位焉。

translations.literal: " He then drafted an abdication edict for the Prince of Anding and yielded the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted the abdication edict for Anding and yielded the throne.

sentences.zh: 戊子，孝武帝即位於東郭之外，用代都舊制，以黑氈蒙七人，歡居其一，帝於氈上西向拜天畢，入御太極殿，群臣朝賀，升閶闔門大赦，改元太昌。

translations.literal: On wuzi Emperor Xiaowu was enthroned outside the eastern gate, using the old customs of the Dai capital: seven men were veiled in black felt, Huan among them; when the emperor had faced west on the felt and worshipped Heaven, he entered and took the throne in the Hall of Supreme Pole. The hundred officials paid court; he ascended the Changhe Gate and proclaimed a general amnesty, changing the era name to Taichang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Emperor Xiaowu was enthroned outside the eastern gate by Dai custom: seven men under black felt, Huan among them; after worshipping Heaven westward on the felt he took the throne, officials bowed, he ascended Changhe Gate, proclaimed amnesty, and changed the era to Taichang.

sentences.zh: 以高歡為大丞相、天柱大將軍、太師，世襲定州刺史。

translations.literal: Gao Huan was made Grand Chancellor, Pillar of State Grand General, and Grand Preceptor, with hereditary Dingzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Huan became grand chancellor, pillar grand general, grand preceptor, and hereditary Dingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，加高澄侍中、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On gengyin Gao Cheng was added as Palace Attendant and Bearer of the Staff with Equal Rank to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Gao Cheng received the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 初，歡起兵信都，爾朱世隆知司馬子如與歡有舊，自侍中、驃騎大將軍出為南岐州刺史。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huan raised troops at Xindu, Erzhu Shilong knew Chief Clerk Ziru was old friends with Huan and sent him from Palace Attendant and General of Agile Cavalry to be Southern Qi Province inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan rose at Xindu, Shilong knew Ziru was Huan's friend and sent him from court to be Southern Qi inspector.

sentences.zh: 歡入洛，召子如為大行台尚書，朝夕左右，參知軍國。

translations.literal: When Huan entered Luoyang he summoned Ziru as Eastern Route Master of Writing and kept him day and night to share in military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Huan summoned Ziru as eastern route master of writing and kept him close in military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 廣州刺史廣寧韓賢，素為歡所善，歡入洛，凡爾朱氏所除官爵例皆削奪，唯賢如故。

translations.literal: Guangzhou inspector Han Xian of Guangning had long been favored by Huan; when Huan entered Luoyang, offices and titles the Erzhu had granted were generally stripped—only Xian remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xian of Guangning, whom Huan favored, kept his offices when others the Erzhu had appointed were stripped.

sentences.zh: 以前御史中尉樊子鵠兼尚書左僕射，為東南道大行台，與徐州刺史杜德追爾朱仲遠，仲遠已出境，遂攻元樹於譙。

translations.literal: Former Chief Censor for Suppressing Evil Fan Zihu was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Southeastern Route Grand Commissioner; with Xuzhou inspector Du De he pursued Erzhu Zhongyuan—Zhongyuan had already left the borders—and then attacked Yuan Shu at Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zihu became left vice director and southeastern commissioner; with Du De he pursued Zhongyuan, then besieged Yuan Shu at Qiao.

sentences.zh: 丞相歡征賀拔岳為冀州刺史，岳畏歡，欲單馬入朝。

translations.literal: Grand Chancellor Huan summoned Heba Yue as Jizhou inspector; Yue feared Huan and wished to enter court alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Huan summoned Heba Yue as Jizhou inspector; Yue feared him and wished to enter court alone.

sentences.zh: 行台右丞薛孝通說岳曰：「高王以數千鮮卑破爾朱百萬之眾，誠亦難敵。

translations.literal: Eastern Route Right Assistant Xue Xiaotong said to Yue, "King Gao with a few thousand Xianbei broke the Erzhu's million—truly hard to match.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Xiaotong told Yue, "King Gao with a few thousand Xianbei broke a million Erzhu—he is formidable.

sentences.zh: 然諸將或素居其上，或與之等夷，雖屈首從之，勢非獲已。

translations.literal: Yet his generals either once ranked above him or were his equals; though they bow their heads and follow, it is not willingly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his generals once ranked above him or were his equals—they follow unwillingly.

sentences.zh: 今或在京師，或據州鎮，高王除之則失人望，留之則為腹心之疾。

translations.literal: Some are in the capital, some hold provinces; if King Gao removes them he loses men's esteem, if he keeps them they are a disease in the vitals.
translations.idiomatic: Remove them and he loses esteem; keep them and they are a disease in the vitals.

sentences.zh: 且吐萬人雖覆敗走，猶在并州，高王方內撫群雄，外抗勍敵，安能去其巢穴，與公爭關中之地乎！

translations.literal: Moreover Tuwu Ren though defeated still holds Bingzhou; King Gao is pacifying heroes within and resisting strong foes without—how can he leave his nest to contend with you for Guanzhong!
translations.idiomatic: Tuwu Ren still holds Bingzhou; Huan cannot leave his nest to fight you for Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 今關中豪俊皆屬心於公，願效其智力。

translations.literal: Now the heroes of Guanzhong all turn their hearts to you and wish to offer their wit and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong's heroes turn to you and offer their strength.

sentences.zh: 公以華山為城，黃河為塹，進可以兼山東，退可以封函谷，奈何欲束手受制於人乎！

translations.literal: Take Mount Hua as your wall and the Yellow River as your moat; advance and you can take Shandong, retreat and you can seal Hangu Pass—why wish to bind your hands and be controlled by others!"
translations.idiomatic: Take Mount Hua and the Yellow River as your defenses—advance to take Shandong, retreat to hold Hangu—why submit to another!"

sentences.zh: 」言未卒，岳執孝通手曰：「君言是也。

translations.literal: Before he finished Yue seized Xiaotong's hand and said, "Your words are right."
translations.idiomatic: Yue seized Xiaotong's hand: "You are right."

sentences.zh: 」乃遜辭為啟而不就征。

translations.literal: " He then declined politely in a memorial and did not accept the summons.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the summons in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，丞相歡還鄴，送爾朱度律、天光於洛陽，斬之。

translations.literal: On renchen Grand Chancellor Huan returned to Ye, sent Erzhu Dulu and Tianguang to Luoyang, and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Huan returned to Ye, sent Dulu and Tianguang to Luoyang, and executed them.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙申，魏主鴆節閔帝於門下外省，詔百司會喪，葬用殊禮。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on bingshen the Wei emperor poisoned Emperor Jiemin in the outer office of the Gate Department and ordered the hundred offices to attend the mourning; burial used special rites.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen the emperor poisoned Jiemin in the Gate Department outer office and ordered state mourning with special burial.

sentences.zh: 以沛郡王欣為太師，趙郡王諶為太保，南陽王寶炬為太尉，長孫稚為太傅。

translations.literal: Prince of Pei Xin was made Grand Preceptor, Prince of Zhao Chen Grand Guardian, Prince of Nanyang Baoju Grand Marshal, and Changsun Zhi Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pei Xin became grand preceptor, Prince of Zhao Chen grand guardian, Prince of Nanyang Baoju grand marshal, and Changsun Zhi grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 寶炬，愉之子也。

translations.literal: Baoju was a son of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Baoju was Yu's son.

sentences.zh: 丞相歡固辭天柱大將軍，戊戌，許之。

translations.literal: Grand Chancellor Huan firmly declined Pillar of State Grand General; on wuxu this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Huan declined pillar grand general; on wuxu the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 己酉，清河王但為司徒。

translations.literal: On jiyou Prince of Qinghe Dan was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Prince of Qinghe Dan became Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 侍中河南高隆之，本徐氏養子，丞相歡命以為弟，恃歡勢驕狎公卿，南陽王寶炬毆之，曰：「鎮兵何敢爾！

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Gao Longzhi of Henan was originally an adopted son of the Xu clan; Grand Chancellor Huan ordered him treated as a younger brother. Trusting Huan's power he was insolent toward the nobles; Prince of Nanyang Baoju beat him, saying, "How dare the garrison soldier act thus!"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Longzhi of Henan, an adopted Xu, Huan's sworn brother, insulted the nobles; Baoju beat him: "How dare a garrison soldier!"

sentences.zh: 」魏主以歡故，六月，丁犯，黜寶炬為驃騎大將軍，歸第。

translations.literal: " Because of Huan, sixth month, on dingfan, Baoju was demoted to General of Agile Cavalry and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: For Huan's sake Baoju was demoted on dingfan and sent home.

sentences.zh: 魏主避廣平武穆王之諱，改謚武懷皇帝曰孝莊皇帝，廟號敬宗。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor avoided the taboo name of Prince of Guangping Wu Mu and changed the posthumous title of Emperor Wu Huai to Emperor Xiaozhuang, temple name Emperor Jingzong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor avoided Guangping Wu Mu's taboo and renamed Wu Huai as Xiaozhuang, temple name Jingzong.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庚子，魏復以南陽王寶炬為太尉。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on gengzi Wei again made Prince of Nanyang Baoju Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Baoju was again made grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，魏丞相歡引兵入滏口，大都督庫狄干入井陘，擊爾朱兆。

translations.literal: On renyin Wei Grand Chancellor Huan led troops into Fukou; Grand Commander Kudigan Gan entered Jingxing to attack Erzhu Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Huan entered Fukou; Kudigan Gan entered Jingxing against Zhao.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，魏主使驃騎大將軍、儀同三司高隆之帥步騎十萬會丞相歡於太原，因以隆之為丞相軍司。

translations.literal: On gengxu the Wei emperor sent General of Agile Cavalry and Staff Equal to the Three Dukes Gao Longzhi with one hundred thousand foot and horse to join Grand Chancellor Huan at Taiyuan, and made Longzhi the chancellor's army marshal.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Longzhi with one hundred thousand men joined Huan at Taiyuan as army marshal.

sentences.zh: 歡軍於武鄉，爾朱兆大掠晉陽，北走秀容。

translations.literal: Huan encamped at Wuxiang; Erzhu Zhao plundered Jinyang greatly and fled north to Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: Huan camped at Wuxiang; Zhao plundered Jinyang and fled to Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 并州平。

translations.literal: Bingzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 歡以晉陽四塞，乃建大丞相府而居之。

translations.literal: Huan, because Jinyang was closed on four sides, built the great chancellor's residence and dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: Huan built the great chancellor's residence at Jinyang and dwelt there.

sentences.zh: 魏夏州遷民郭遷據青州反，刺史元嶷棄城走。

translations.literal: Wei migrants of Xiazhou: Guo Qian seized Qingzhou in rebellion; inspector Yuan Yi abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qian of Xiazhou migrants seized Qingzhou; Yuan Yi fled.

sentences.zh: 詔行台侯景等討之，拔其城，遷來奔。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Eastern Route Commissioner Hou Jing and others to attack him, took the city, and Qian came over in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing and others took the city; Qian fled to surrender.

sentences.zh: 魏東南道大行台樊子鵠圍元樹於譙城，分兵攻取蒙縣等五城，以絕援兵之路。

translations.literal: Wei Southeastern Route Grand Commissioner Fan Zihu besieged Yuan Shu at Qiaocheng, sent troops to take Meng county and five other cities to cut off relief.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zihu besieged Yuan Shu at Qiao and took five cities to cut relief.

sentences.zh: 樹請帥眾南歸，以地還魏，子鵠等許之，與之誓約。

translations.literal: Shu asked to lead his host south and return the land to Wei; Zihu and the others agreed and swore an oath with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shu asked to go south and return the land; Zihu agreed under oath.

sentences.zh: 樹眾半出，子鵠擊之，擒樹及譙州刺史朱文開以歸。

translations.literal: When half Shu's host had come out, Zihu struck them and captured Shu and Qiao inspector Zhu Wenkai and brought them back.
translations.idiomatic: When half his men were out, Zihu struck, captured Shu and Zhu Wenkai, and returned.

sentences.zh: 羊侃行至官竹，聞樹敗而還。

translations.literal: Yang Kan reached Guanzhu, heard Shu was defeated, and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Kan reached Guanzhu, heard of the defeat, and returned.

sentences.zh: 九月，樹至洛陽，久之，復欲南奔，魏人殺之。

translations.literal: Ninth month: Shu reached Luoyang; long after, he again wished to flee south and the Wei men killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Shu reached Luoyang; later he tried to flee south and was killed.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以司空袁昂領尚書令。

translations.literal: On yisi Minister of Works Yuan Ang was put in charge of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Yuan Ang headed the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，丁酉，日南至，魏主祀圜丘。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month, on dingyou, the winter solstice; the Wei emperor sacrificed at the Round Altar.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, winter solstice, the emperor sacrificed at the Round Altar.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，魏殺安定王朗、東海王曄。

translations.literal: On jiachen Wei executed Prince of Anding Lang and Prince of Donghai Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen Wei executed Princes Lang and Ye.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以汝南王悅為侍中、大司馬。

translations.literal: On jiyou Prince of Runan Yue was made Palace Attendant and Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Prince of Runan Yue became palace attendant and grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 魏葬靈太后胡氏。

translations.literal: Wei buried Empress Dowager Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei buried Empress Dowager Hu.

sentences.zh: 上聞魏室已定，十二月，庚辰，復以太尉元法僧為郢州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor heard the Wei house was settled; twelfth month, on gengchen, again made Grand Marshal Yuan Faseng Yingzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Wei was settled, on gengchen the emperor again made Faseng Yingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 魏主以汝南王悅屬近地尊，丁亥，殺之。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor, because Prince of Runan Yue was close kin and honored locally, on dinghai killed him.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai the emperor killed Yue as too close in kin and local honor.

sentences.zh: 魏大赦，改元永興；

translations.literal: Wei proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Yongxing;
translations.idiomatic: Wei proclaimed amnesty and the era Yongxing;

sentences.zh: 以與太宗同號，復改永熙。

translations.literal: because it shared the name with Emperor Taizong, it was again changed to Yongxi.
translations.idiomatic: then changed it to Yongxi to avoid Taizong's name.

sentences.zh: 魏主納丞相歡女為後，命太常卿李元忠納幣於晉陽。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor took Grand Chancellor Huan's daughter as empress and ordered Minister of Ceremonies Li Yuanzhong to present betrothal gifts at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor married Huan's daughter and sent Li Yuanzhong with betrothal gifts to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 歡與之宴，論及舊事，元忠曰：「昔日建義，轟轟大樂，比來寂寂無人問。

translations.literal: Huan feasted with him and spoke of old affairs. Yuanzhong said, "In those days when we raised the righteous cause, music thundered; since then it has been silent—no one asks."
translations.idiomatic: At the feast Yuanzhong said, "When we raised the righteous cause the music thundered; since then, silence."

sentences.zh: 」歡撫掌笑曰：「此人逼我起兵。

translations.literal: " Huan clapped his hands and laughed, "This man drove me to raise troops."
translations.idiomatic: Huan laughed, "This man drove me to rebel."

sentences.zh: 」元忠戲曰：「若不與侍中，當更求建義處。

translations.literal: " Yuanzhong jested, "If you will not give me Palace Attendant, I shall seek another place to raise the righteous cause."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong jested, "Without the palace attendant post I shall find another place to rebel."

sentences.zh: 」歡曰：「建義不慮無，止畏如此老翁不可遇耳。

translations.literal: " Huan said, "Places to raise the cause are not lacking—I only fear such an old fellow cannot be met again."
translations.idiomatic: Huan said, "Rebellion is easy to find—I fear I shall not meet such an old fellow again."

sentences.zh: 」元忠曰：「止為此翁難遇，所以不去。

translations.literal: " Yuanzhong said, "It is because such an old fellow is hard to meet that I do not leave."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong said, "Because you are hard to meet, I stay."

sentences.zh: 」因捋歡須大笑。

translations.literal: " He then tugged Huan's beard and laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He tugged Huan's beard and laughed.

sentences.zh: 歡悉其雅意，深重之。

translations.literal: Huan understood his refined intent and valued him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Huan understood and valued him deeply.

sentences.zh: 爾朱兆既至秀容，分守險隘，出入寇抄。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao reached Xiurong he held the passes and raided in and out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao reached Xiurong, held the passes, and raided.

sentences.zh: 魏丞相歡揚聲討之，師出復止者數四，兆意怠。

translations.literal: Wei Grand Chancellor Huan proclaimed he would attack him; several times the army set out and stopped again, and Zhao grew slack.
translations.idiomatic: Huan proclaimed war, marched out and halted several times, and Zhao grew slack.

sentences.zh: 歡揣其歲首當宴會，遣都督竇泰以精騎馳之，一日一夜行三百里，歡以大軍繼之。

translations.literal: Huan guessed that at the year's start there would be a feast; he sent Commander Dou Tai with picked horse to rush there—three hundred li in one day and night—and Huan followed with the great army.
translations.idiomatic: Huan guessed a New Year feast; he sent Dou Tai three hundred li in a day and night, and followed with the main army.

translations.idiomatic: Category: Zizhi Tongjian
